counters.tier: Tier 1 (June 2026 meta; most-represented deck at YCS Columbus, full-power in Master Duel as of April 2026)
counters.game_plan: Kewl Tune is an almost-all-Tuner Synchro toolbox that uses the "Hand Synchro" mechanic: on-field Kewl Tune monsters let you use Tuners from your HAND as Synchro material, so it climbs to bosses with very few cards and rarely bricks. It abuses information asymmetry (Rotary peeks the opponent's hand, Cue/Crackle manipulate the opponent's draw and Extra Deck), then ends on the omni-negate boss Zalen plus a Kewl Tune Synchro held in hand for "Turn 0" disruption on the opponent's turn. It adapts its end board to exactly what it saw in your hand, making it a control deck that knows your outs before you draw them.

key_cards.role: Primary starter. Normal Summon recruits any Tuner from Deck and can manipulate the opponent's next draw; the core 1-card line begins here.
Information engine. Reveals the opponent's hand turn 1 so the deck tailors its negates to your specific hand traps and breakers.
GY recursion + Turn-0 Synchro. Recovers Tuners (including used hand traps) from GY and can Synchro Summon during the opponent's turn. This is why GY shutdown hurts so much.
Quick-Effect 'Hand Synchro' enabler. Lets the deck Synchro Summon on the opponent's turn for reactive interaction; the backbone of their going-first disruption.
Main boss. A tricky omni-negate that is built to play around chain blocking; also negates Ash Blossom aimed at their searches. The card you must answer to win.
Held-in-hand interaction piece. Chained to your disruption (e.g. Nibiru) so they can then resolve Zalen's negate; key to how they survive going first.

interruption_points.timing: On the Normal Summon of Kewl Tune Cue (the search)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom or Droll here is the cleanest stop, BUT be aware an established Zalen negates Ash. If they have no negate up yet, denying the first search slows the line dramatically.

interruption_points.timing: Before / during the first 1-2 Synchro Summons (the climb)
interruption_points.action: Imperm/Veiler on the on-field Hand-Synchro monster is weak: they simply Hand-Synchro using a DIFFERENT Tuner from hand. Aim disruption at the SEARCH/recursion engine, not the climbing monster.

interruption_points.timing: On a second/third search or special summon (heavy chain)
interruption_points.action: Droll & Lock Bird freezes the heavy searching chain after the first search, often crippling extension. One of the few single hand traps that meaningfully stops them.

interruption_points.timing: At the 5th total summon of the turn
interruption_points.action: Nibiru window. They mitigate by ending before summon 5 or by making/holding Zalen + Kewl Tune Synchro to chain-negate the Nibiru. Effective only if they over-extended without a negate ready.

interruption_points.timing: When Zalen tries to omni-negate your play
interruption_points.action: Zalen's negate only protects the 2 most recent chain links. Bait it, then chain a SECOND effect as CL3 when priority returns to you so your real CL1 effect resolves around it.

hand_traps.when: Drawn turn 1, activate before they start (ideally going second, or in response to first effect).
hand_traps.why: Best single counter. Banishing-instead-of-GY shuts off Kewl Tune Remix's GY recovery of Tuners/used hand traps, which is core to their grind and Turn-0 plays. Dimensional Fissure / Macro Cosmos do similar work.

hand_traps.when: After their FIRST search resolves (do not waste it before any search).
hand_traps.why: Freezes the search-heavy chains the deck relies on to extend; one of the very few single hand traps that can stop the combo outright. Note they may chain-block it, so timing matters.

hand_traps.when: Turn 1 before they commit, mainly Master Duel.
hand_traps.why: Punishes the special-summon-heavy line; even if they 'play around' it, they often must short-stop the combo. In TCG it is banned; relevant in Master Duel only. Expect them to fight it with Called by / Crossout.

hand_traps.when: On Cue's first search, before any negate is established.
hand_traps.why: Stops the opening search, but loses value once Zalen is up (Zalen negates Ash on their searches). Best as an early-window answer, not a save vs an established board.

hand_traps.when: Held until their 5th summon of the turn.
hand_traps.why: Wipes an over-extended board, but they actively play around it (stop at summon 4, or chain Kewl Tune Synchro -> Zalen to negate). Treat as a punish for greedy lines, not a guaranteed stop.

hand_traps.card: Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit / Effect Veiler / Infinite Impermanence
hand_traps.when: Veiler/Imperm on a Hand-Synchro monster's on-field effect; Ogre on a key Synchro.
hand_traps.why: Weakest options. Negating one on-field Tuner just lets them Hand-Synchro with another Tuner from hand; Imperm/Dark Ruler does not stop the core mechanic. Use only to bait or as backup, not your main answer.

hand_traps.card: Herald-type / Fairy hand traps (e.g. Herald of Orange Light)
hand_traps.when: Going second, to protect your own Shifter/Droll/Maxx from their Ash/Crossout.
hand_traps.why: Used to defend your key hand traps from being Crossout/Called/Ashed, since the deck sees your hand and targets your best out first.

board_breakers.why: Going second, forces out Zalen's negate and can clear their backrow/attack-position monsters. Caveat: needs a near-empty field of your own to activate, so lead with it before committing.
Strong going second since you end with no cards; they keep only one card. Also baits/eats the omni-negate. Same empty-field-side requirement as Lightning Storm.
Clears their backrow support (Playlist / continuous traps / field spell layer) cheaply; pair with a follow-up to push through Zalen.
Tribute away Zalen (and Synchro bosses) ignoring its negate, since tributing is not an effect they can stop. Reliable single-card answer to the omni-negate body.
Negates Zalen plus other monsters at once; cost (sending cards) is acceptable to open a push. Good multi-negate disabler before your main play.
Uncounterable in chain (they can't respond), removes their Synchro material(s) and bypasses Zalen. Note they often MAIN their own Super Poly, so watch for the mirror.

board_breakers.card: Dimensional Fissure / Macro Cosmos (floodgate breakers post-board)
board_breakers.why: Not a one-time clear but neuters the rebuild: shutting off GY stops Remix from recovering their pieces after you break the board, so your push sticks.

counters.going_first_vs_second: GOING FIRST is their preferred line: they set Zalen + a held Kewl Tune Synchro/Clip for Turn-0 interaction and read your hand via Rotary, then negate your single best out. To beat them on the draw, you must end on MULTIPLE threats/negates, not one, because they tailor disruption to whatever they saw. GOING SECOND, they still threaten Turn-0 Hand Synchro (Clip/Remix make Synchros on your turn), so do not assume an empty board is safe; lead with going-second breakers (Evenly/Lightning Storm) BEFORE summoning, use Super Poly/Kaiju to ignore Zalen, and protect your key hand trap (Shifter/Droll) from Crossout/Ash with Herald-type cards. Mulligan toward Shifter, Droll, or a board breaker + a way to bait the negate.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Kewl Tune as a deck of all "Tuners" that builds Synchro monsters using cards from its HAND, so it almost never bricks, and it cheats by looking at your hand and even your draws. The one card you really must answer is its boss Zalen (a negate). Rule of thumb: do not waste Effect Veiler/Impermanence on their little monsters, they just use a different card from hand instead. Your best plain-English plan: (1) if you have Dimension Shifter, use it early, it shuts off their recycling; (2) Droll & Lock Bird right after their first search is a great stop; (3) hold Nibiru for their 5th monster of the turn, but know they may dodge it; (4) when going second, swing with Lightning Storm or Evenly Matched FIRST while your field is empty, or use a Kaiju/Super Polymerization to remove Zalen since those ignore its negate. Bait their negate with a throwaway play, then do your real play.

counters.game_plan: Spam Fusion Summons off one starter (usually Branded Fusion) to assemble a grindy board headlined by Mirrorjade the Iceblade Dragon (quick-effect non-targeting banish) plus a quickplay spell and often a Dogmatika negate. It recurs materials from GY/banish, so it grinds you out over multiple turns rather than going for a single huge OTK. Going second it pivots to Branded in Red / Super Poly OTK lines.

key_cards.role: #1 starter and main chokepoint. Sends Albaz + Bystial Lubellion (or Despia) from deck to summon Albion the Branded Dragon, which chains into Lubellion the Searing Dragon and the whole engine. Stop this and the turn often collapses.
Secondary starter. On summon searches any Branded card, almost always Branded Fusion. Negating Aluber cuts off the deck's access to its starter when they don't already have it.
Core Fusion material / extender. Albaz fuses with opponent's monsters (and powers Super Poly); Bystial Lubellion self-revives by sending Albion, extending past one interruption.
The pivot Fusion. Banishes Albaz + a Branded card to summon Lubellion the Searing Dragon and sets up loops; its GY effect sets a Branded card for next turn.
The payoff / main interruption. Once per turn quick-effect SENDS a monster to GY (non-targeting banish-tier removal). This is the card you usually need to play around or out-resource.
Field Spell engine. Extra Fusion Summon and revives a Fusion destroyed by battle/effect. Adds resilience, not the thing to negate first.
Common board piece providing a non-targeting monster effect negate on your turn. Plan your push around one negate.

interruption_points.timing: On Branded Fusion activation (the fusion summon)
interruption_points.action: This is THE chokepoint. Negate / disrupt here. Without a backup starter or extra Albaz access, the turn usually dies. Best single point to spend Ash.

interruption_points.timing: On Aluber the Jester of Despia summon (search effect)
interruption_points.action: Negate the search to deny Branded Fusion access, but ONLY if they don't already have Branded Fusion in hand and have no GY recursion (Branded Retribution / Despian Tragedy / Albion GY set).

interruption_points.timing: On Albion the Branded Dragon's effect (banish to summon Lubellion the Searing Dragon)
interruption_points.action: Stops the chain into Lubellion and the recursion loop. Veiler / Imperm here is strong since Albion is the engine pivot.

interruption_points.timing: After ~5 summons in their turn
interruption_points.action: Nibiru window. Branded does many summons; if they over-extend before resolving Mirrorjade, Nibiru wipes the board. They can play around it by leading with Mirrorjade early, so timing matters.

interruption_points.timing: On the second Branded search / second Special Summon engine activation
interruption_points.action: Droll & Lock Bird window. Branded leans on searching and adding multiple cards from deck per turn, so Droll mid-combo strands their hand.

hand_traps.when: On Branded Fusion (best), or on Aluber's search if they lack Branded Fusion + GY recursion.
hand_traps.why: Negates the #1 starter at its activation. Devastating against a hand with no extender; the engine cannot continue. Read whether they have backup before choosing the target.

hand_traps.when: On Albaz/Albion/Lubellion engine monster, or on Mirrorjade to disable its banish during your push.
hand_traps.why: Veiler/Imperm shut down the pivot monster's effect (no chain into the next fusion). Imperm doubles as your-turn removal of Mirrorjade's negate. Note: Imperm column restriction matters going second.

hand_traps.when: After they make 5+ summons but BEFORE they lock in Mirrorjade.
hand_traps.why: Branded summons a lot, so the window usually opens. Wipes the whole board into one token. Weakness: good players sequence Mirrorjade early to dodge it, so it is not a guaranteed answer.

hand_traps.when: After their first add-to-hand (e.g. after the first search), to brick the rest of the combo.
hand_traps.why: Branded chains multiple adds/searches per turn; Droll strands their hand once you cut further adds. One of the harder hand traps for them to play through.

hand_traps.when: On Despia, Theater of the Branded (field spell) or on a key engine Fusion when its effect resolves.
hand_traps.why: Destroys the field spell engine or a board piece, costing them an extra summon/recur. Decent but not as backbreaking as Ash on Branded Fusion.

hand_traps.when: Before they start summoning (in MD especially).
hand_traps.why: Punishes the multi-summon turn. Branded CAN play through it by stopping early on a Mirrorjade end board, so it is a tax/deterrent more than a hard stop. Banned/limited in TCG; mainly an MD consideration.

board_breakers.why: Best dedicated answer. Their board is DARK/dragon Fusions; Super Poly fuses Mirrorjade and others away into your fusion, and its activation cannot be responded to. Branded itself plays it, so it's a known weakness.
Negates AND lowers ATK of multiple monsters at once, including Mirrorjade, opening the board for an attack. Strong going second; pitching cards is the cost.
Going second into a board of face-up monsters (and no spells/traps set), wipes all their attack-position monsters including Mirrorjade. Dead if they have a set backrow up.
End-of-your-turn or going second, forces them to banish down to one card. Excellent against their wide grind board since it ignores effects.
Clears the quickplay spell(s) Branded leaves up (Branded in Red / removal / Branded Retribution), removing their disruption before you push.
Tribute away Mirrorjade (gets around its 'cannot be destroyed' style protection by sending/tributing instead of destroying), neutralizing the key threat so you can attack over the rest.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Against you going FIRST: their threat is Mirrorjade's quick banish plus a possible Dogmatika negate, so end on a board that survives one removal and one negate; bait the negate with a non-essential effect, then commit your real play. Hold an interrupt for their follow-up turn since they grind. Against you going SECOND: expect Mirrorjade + a quickplay + sometimes a negate. Lead with a board breaker (Super Poly / Droplet / Evenly / Feather Duster / Kaiju) to clear BEFORE you combo, and respect a possible set Branded card. Hand traps are far better in the going-first matchup; going second, prioritize breakers over reactive traps.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Branded as a deck that starts almost everything from ONE card, Branded Fusion, and you usually want to stop that exact card. If they activate Branded Fusion, that is the moment to drop Ash Blossom. If they search with Aluber first, Ash can hit that instead, but only if you think they don't already have Branded Fusion. Their scariest finished monster is Mirrorjade, which can banish one of your monsters whenever it wants, so don't dump your whole hand into a board it can pick apart. If you are going second and they already have a board, do NOT try to out-combo them, just blow up the board first with a card like Super Polymerization, Forbidden Droplet, Lightning Storm, or a Kaiju, THEN make your plays. Watch out: they can play through a single hand trap and through Maxx C by stopping early, so one interruption is often not enough, save the right one for the right card.

counters.archetype: DoomZ (DARK Dragon main deck / WIND Machine Xyz boss). Note: card names appear with translation variants (Drastia/Drastea, Amalthe/Amarut, Elara/Erara). Boss = DoomZ XII End - Drastrius.
counters.game_plan: Self-destruction combo deck: it destroys its own DoomZ cards to trigger searches, special summons, and free spell/trap setting, then converts monsters into WIND Machine Xyz. Goal is to end on the Rank 8 boss Drastrius (a monster-effect omni-negate that also steals your monster as an equip) plus the DoomZ Destruction floodgate trap and assorted equip-based protection. It is a resource-looping deck that floats through disruption rather than going wide.

key_cards.role: End-board boss. Rank 8 WIND Machine Xyz (2700 ATK). Quick-effect negate of opponent monster effects on FIELD or GY, then equips (steals) one of your monsters. Survives first destruction each turn. CRITICAL LIMIT: it cannot negate hand-activated effects, so Nibiru and hand traps still resolve during their combo.
Primary 1-card starter. Destroys a DoomZ monster (e.g. Amalthe/Amarut) from Deck to start the search-and-summon chain. Prime Ash Blossom / Droll target.
Level 4 DARK Dragon. When destroyed/sent it searches/adds DoomZ pieces (notably Drastia) from Deck. Ash Blossom hits this GY search. Veiler/Imperm can stop it on field.
Level 8 DARK Dragon. Self-Special-Summons by destroying a DoomZ card; equips and converts into a same-Rank WIND Machine Xyz (the bridge to Drastrius). Veiler/Imperm shuts it off.
Level 4 DARK Dragon Normal-Summon starter. On summon/destruction sets DoomZ spell/trap from Deck or extends. Alternative single-card opener.

Level 1 WIND Machine. Floodgate/enabler: restricts Extra Deck summons to Xyz only and converts effect monsters into Xyz. Part of the engine and a self-imposed lock you can exploit (they cannot make non-Xyz plays).
Normal Trap floodgate on the end board. Prevents opponent from adding cards from Main Deck to hand except by drawing; floats a DoomZ monster as equip when destroyed. Soft floodgate, not a negate.

interruption_points.timing: On the opening DoomZ Change activation / the destroy-from-Deck cost
interruption_points.action: This is the 1-card-combo ignition. Ash Blossom the resulting Deck-to-hand search (Amalthe/Drastia add). Droll & Lock Bird here shuts off all further Deck searches for the turn.

interruption_points.timing: On Amalthe/Amarut's GY add-from-Deck trigger
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom negates the search and chokes the line at its weakest link. Crossout the Ash if you fear they have Called by/Crossout themselves.

interruption_points.timing: On Drastia/Drastea's self-Special-Summon and equip/Xyz-conversion
interruption_points.action: Effect Veiler or Infinite Impermanence on Drastia stops the climb into the Rank 8 Xyz. This is the cleanest spot for a negate-on-field hand trap.

interruption_points.timing: After they have Special Summoned 5+ monsters this turn (extended lines only)
interruption_points.action: Nibiru, the Primal Being tributes their board. Works because Drastrius negates only FIELD/GY effects, never hand effects. Note: the streamlined DoomZ Change line may only make ~2 summons, so Nibiru can whiff vs the short combo.

interruption_points.timing: Before/while they set up the floodgate
interruption_points.action: Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit can destroy a key Xyz/equipped piece or a continuous DoomZ spell, or detach material so Drastrius's negate runs dry.

hand_traps.why: Hits the core engine: DoomZ Change's destroy-search, Amalthe's GY add-from-Deck, or any DoomZ Deck-to-hand/Deck-summon effect. Single best one-card answer.
hand_traps.when: Hold for the FIRST add-from-Deck or SS-from-Deck of the combo (usually DoomZ Change or Amalthe).

hand_traps.why: Drastrius and the whole archetype have NO hand-activated negation, so Nibiru resolves freely. Wipes the board after the 5th summon.
hand_traps.when: Only when they cross 5 summons. Count carefully: the short DoomZ Change line can stop at ~2 SS and dodge it. Better vs the extended Elara/pendulum line.

hand_traps.why: After their first search, Droll locks out every further Deck-add for the turn, collapsing a deck that chains multiple searches.
hand_traps.when: Activate after they resolve the first search (let DoomZ Change add, then Droll the next add).

hand_traps.why: Negates Drastia/Amalthe on the field, breaking the bridge into the Rank 8 boss.
hand_traps.when: On Drastia's self-summon/conversion effect, or on Amalthe if it triggers on field.

hand_traps.why: Same role as Veiler plus it works going second and can stop a spell/trap column. Strong on the normal-summoned starter (Elara) or Drastia.
hand_traps.when: On the first DoomZ monster effect resolving on the field; set it pre-emptively going second for the column-negate upside.

hand_traps.why: Punishes the special-summon-heavy combo; forces them to either over-draw you or stop short of the full board.
hand_traps.when: Activate at the very start of their turn before they commit. Beware Called by/Crossout in their build.

hand_traps.why: Destroys a just-summoned Xyz, an equipped DoomZ piece, or detaches/removes a continuous spell, weakening Drastrius's negate fuel.
hand_traps.when: On the Xyz summon or on a continuous DoomZ spell/equip activation during the combo.

hand_traps.why: Floods you with cards off their special summons (mirroring what their own lists run), keeping your board-breaker hand stocked going second.
hand_traps.when: Start of their turn if you have no other interaction and expect to go second next.

board_breakers.why: Top answer. Sends fodder to halve ATK and NEGATE Drastrius and other DoomZ monsters at once; the chain-restriction prevents them from responding to the rest of your turn. Note Drastrius survives one destruction but Droplet negates rather than destroys.
If they leave Drastrius in attack position with no other backrow protecting, blow up all their attack-position monsters, or wipe their set DoomZ Destruction in spell/trap mode.
Going second with an empty field, force them to banish down to one card. Cleanly answers the floating equip-heavy board that grinds back from spot removal.

Spell-speed-4, chain-restricted fusion that eats Drastrius (or the equipped monster) regardless of its negate; also pre-empts them stealing your monster. Many DoomZ lists main it themselves, so respect the mirror.
Tribute-summon away Drastrius ignoring its 'not destroyed' protection and its negate (Kaiju is a tribute, not destruction/targeting-negate trigger they can stop).
Removes the DoomZ Destruction floodgate trap and any equip-spell protection so your follow-up resolves; Duster clears the whole backrow.

board_breakers.card: Dark Ruler No More / Forbidden Droplet (negate-all line)
board_breakers.why: DRNM turns off all their monster negates (Drastrius included) for the turn so you can push without eating the omni-negate, then OTK through the now-passive board.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going FIRST against them: race to resolve your own disruption; on YOUR turn deploy hand traps the moment they ignite DoomZ Change/Elara. Their board is a single monster-negate (Drastrius) plus a soft floodgate, so a clean Ash or Veiler at the right link often stops the whole thing. If you are the DoomZ player's opponent and YOU got first, set up a backrow they have to fight through and keep Nibiru/Droll for their combo turn. Going SECOND against them: their ceiling is low (one omni-negate, no hand disruption), so a single good board breaker usually breaks it. Lead with a negate-all (Dark Ruler No More) or chain-locked removal (Forbidden Droplet / Super Polymerization) to bypass Drastrius, then clear the DoomZ Destruction floodgate with Duster/Cosmic before committing your main play. Save Evenly Matched if you can bait them into a full board. Because Drastrius can STEAL one of your monsters as equip, avoid feeding it a strong monster; remove it before you over-extend.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of DoomZ as a deck that blows up its own cards on purpose to fetch more cards and summon a big WIND machine boss called Drastrius. That boss can negate ONE of your monster effects per turn and even take your monster, but here is the trick a beginner needs to know: Drastrius can only stop effects you use from your FIELD or GRAVEYARD, never from your HAND. So your hand traps (Ash Blossom, Nibiru, Veiler, Imperm) are safe to use during their setup. The simplest plan: hold Ash Blossom for the very first time they search a card off DoomZ Change (their main combo button) and that usually stalls them hard. If you are going second and they already have the board, do not trade a single removal into Drastrius (it survives one destruction); instead use a card that negates or fusion-eats it like Forbidden Droplet, Super Polymerization, or a Kaiju you can tribute it away with, then clear their face-down DoomZ Destruction trap with Harpie's Feather Duster. Their board looks scary but only has one real negate, so one good breaker plus one hand trap is often enough.

counters.game_plan: Fusion-summon engine that uses Main Deck Dracotail monsters as fusion material to Set disruptive Dracotail Spells/Traps straight from the deck, then grind. It builds a layered control board (a negating fusion like Gulamel plus 2-3 recursive traps: Flame negates a Spell, Horn bounces an Attack-position monster, Sting banishes from GY) while every Dracotail effect feeds Gulamel's destruction. Faimena gives it a "turn 0" Quick-Effect fusion to interrupt you on your own turn, and Arthalion bounces your board while recycling its own resources, so it wins by out-resourcing and out-grinding rather than by one big negate wall.

key_cards.role: Best 1-card starter. Normal Summon searches Mululu, which fuses into Gulamel and Sets two traps. If you see Lukias Normal Summoned, the combo has begun.
Quick-Effect from hand that triggers the fusion into Gulamel; also permanently negates a monster. The card that turns Lukias into a board.

Discard from hand as a Quick Effect (either player's Main Phase) to Fusion Summon a Dragon/Spellcaster. Their turn-0 interruption AND extender. Sets a Dracotail S/T when used as fusion material. Recognize this as the scariest card to leave them holding.
Main search Spell: adds a Dracotail monster; if you control a monster it also Fusion Summons. The consistency glue, hits on Ash Blossom.
Dedicated Fusion Spell using materials from the deck; locks them into Extra Deck Fusion Summons for the turn. 1-card board enabler, prime Ash/Called by/Ghost Ogre target.
Fusion that bounces field/GY monsters to hand equal to materials used from hand. Their main board breaker going second and a tempo swing turn 1.
End-board fusion: Quick Effect destroys an opponent card every time a Dracotail card/effect activates. The disruption multiplier you must respect.
Engine extender/starter that can be sent to set up the Dracotail line; targets Lukias to extend.

interruption_points.timing: On Dracotail Lukias Normal Summon (search for Mululu)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the search to cut the 1-card starter off at the knees. This is the cleanest stop on the most common opener.

interruption_points.timing: On Ketu Dracotail or Rahu Dracotail activation
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom (Ketu = search/Fusion; Rahu = Fusion from deck). Negating either kneecaps the consistency/board build. Called by the Grave / Crossout protect these, so bait first if possible.

interruption_points.timing: On the Mululu / Faimena Quick-Effect Fusion Summon
interruption_points.action: Effect Veiler or Infinite Impermanence on Mululu (or the relevant fusion enabler) stops the fusion-and-set chain. Imperm is best set in advance so it survives going second.

interruption_points.timing: After 5 monsters hit the field during their combo
interruption_points.action: Nibiru the Primordial Being tributes the board. Dracotail floods the field with fusion material + tokens, so they routinely hit 5 summons before the end board is locked. Strong blind second.

interruption_points.timing: On any draw/search loop (their effects almost all search or draw)
interruption_points.action: Droll & Lock Bird after their first search shuts off all further adds (Ketu, Lukias, recursion). Note: pros sometimes cut Droll in 2026 because it also clogs your own searchers, so it is a meta call.

interruption_points.timing: On Arthalion's GY-to-hand recycle or Gulamel's destruction loop
interruption_points.action: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion / D.D. Crow to deny GY recursion. D.D. Crow banishing Faimena from GY prevents next-turn Quick-Effect fusing.

hand_traps.when: Chain to Lukias's search, Ketu, or Rahu
hand_traps.why: Almost every Dracotail starter is a search or deck-Fusion. Ash on the first search usually ends the turn. Their single best target. Watch for Called by / Crossout protecting it.

hand_traps.when: On the fusion enabler (Mululu) or on Gulamel/Arthalion when it counts
hand_traps.why: Negating the Quick-Effect fusion stops the trap-setting chain. Imperm doubles as a board breaker going second; set it pre-emptively so it survives backrow removal.

hand_traps.when: Before they start, ideally going first into their turn
hand_traps.why: Dracotail Special Summons a lot (multiple fusions + recursion), so Maxx C draws heavily. But the deck can recycle/draw your used copies and grinds resources, so it is a tempo tax more than a hard stop in MD (where it is legal). Banned in TCG.

hand_traps.when: After their 5th summon, before the end board locks
hand_traps.why: They flood the field with material and tokens, frequently crossing 5 summons. Tributes the board and leaves you a token to push. Premier blind-second card.

hand_traps.when: After they take their first add/search this turn
hand_traps.why: Shuts off the whole search-and-recycle gameplan. Caveat: weak in the 2026 meta generally and clogs your own decks, so many lists cut it. Still very punishing specifically vs Dracotail.

hand_traps.when: On Rahu/Ketu's Fusion, Gulamel, or a Set Dracotail card being activated
hand_traps.why: Flexible: destroys an enabler or a key fusion piece on activation. Less clean than Ash but dodges some protection.

hand_traps.card: D.D. Crow / Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
hand_traps.when: On GY recursion (Arthalion add-back, Faimena in GY)
hand_traps.why: Belle denies Arthalion returning cards from GY (kills their card advantage); Crow banishing Faimena in GY stops the next-turn Quick fusion.

hand_traps.when: Before their combo, going second or as a turn-0 lock
hand_traps.why: Banishing instead of GY shuts off the trap-setting-as-material and GY recursion that the entire engine relies on. Niche but devastating if you can resolve it early.

board_breakers.why: Going second into a defense-position fusion board, it wipes their monsters; if they have backrow up, it nukes the Set Dracotail traps instead. Strong but watch for them activating a Set trap in response.
Best against their wide control board: end of your Battle Phase forces them to banish down to one card. Great because their board is several cards (fusion + 2-3 traps) and they go first often.
Dumps multiple cards to halve ATK and negate effects of their fusions (Gulamel/Arthalion), and the chain-link cost dodges their Set-trap responses. Reliable out to the negating body.
Clears the recursive Dracotail trap layer (Flame/Horn/Sting) in one shot, the part of their board that grinds you out. Best paired with monster removal.
Tributes away the key negating/bouncing fusion (Gulamel, Arthalion) ignoring its protection, then you swing or combo through. Good single-card answer to their boss.
Their board is full of fusion-material Dragons/Spellcasters; SuperPoly removes their boss as material with no response window (no chain to it). One of the cleaner outs to Gulamel.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going first they want 1-2 cards to make Gulamel (or a negating fusion) plus 2-3 Set Dracotail traps, then grind. Going second they lean on Faimena's Quick-Effect fusion as a turn-0 interruption and on Arthalion to bounce your board, so they are dangerous from either seat. Against them: when YOU go first, build a board that survives Arthalion's bounce and a single targeted destruction (avoid relying on one fragile negate, and bait Gulamel before committing). When YOU go second, mulligan toward board breakers (Evenly, Droplet, Duster, SuperPoly, Kaiju) plus a pre-set Imperm, and hold up Nibiru for their flood. Crucially, even on their turn keep Ash up: their turn-0 Faimena and recursion mean the combo is not "over" after turn 1.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Dracotail as a deck that "pays" its small monsters to flip up free trap cards from its deck while building a fusion monster that destroys your stuff. The easiest tell: a Dracotail monster gets Normal Summoned and immediately searches another one, then a fusion appears and they Set 2-3 cards face-down. Your single best button is Ash Blossom on the FIRST search they make (usually Lukias, Ketu, or Rahu) because nearly everything they do is a search or a draw, so cutting the first one off usually ends their turn. Going second, do not try to out-grind them: blow up the whole board at once with a card like Evenly Matched, Harpie's Feather Duster (for the traps), or Forbidden Droplet (for the fusion). And remember Faimena, a card they discard on YOUR turn to make a fusion, so do not relax just because it is your turn. Keep one hand trap up if you can.

counters.game_plan: Elfnote is a Synchro-combo deck built around three Singer monsters (Lucina, Tinia, Fortuna) that special-summon themselves to the Center Main Monster Zone to trigger effects, search each other, and place their own Continuous Spell (Welcome Home) and Continuous Trap (Rhapsodia of Madness). It Synchro-climbs through Elfnote Power Patron (a Tuner that searches any Elfnote card when used as Synchro material) to end on generic boss Synchros like Baronne de Fleur plus Crystal Wing, backed by the Center-zone lock, a spell/trap negate, and on-turn handrip. The board grinds: it protects the center monster from destruction and recurs Elfnotes from GY during your turn.

key_cards.role: Main starter. Hard-OPT searches any Elfnote monster (except another Lucina); during your turn moves to Center MMZ to random-banish from your hand. Top Ash/Imperm target.

The engine glue: Tuner that Synchro-climbs (raise a Center monster's Level by 3, then Synchro Summon), and when sent as Synchro material adds ANY Elfnote card from deck. Removing it cuts them off Synchros.
Places Elfnotes: Welcome Home (Continuous Spell) from deck and random-banishes from opponent hand. Combo extender/searcher.
Places Elfnotes: Rhapsodia of Madness (Continuous Trap) from deck and bounces opponent S/T. Sets up the negate.

Their main disruption: locks opponent attacks to the Center monster, recurs an Elfnote from GY + negates 1 face-up card (if they control a Synchro), and negates opponent S/T while controlling 3+ Elfnotes.
Continuous Spell: makes the Center monster destruction-immune to effects and recurs Elfnotes from deck. Why pure destruction removal underperforms.
Generic boss Synchros that cap the board (omni-negate-and-destroy / monster-effect negate). The actual end-board interruptions you must answer.

interruption_points.timing: On the first Elfnote search (Lucina/Tinia/Medius effect resolving in the early Main Phase, before they build the field)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the search to deny the engine piece. Cleanest single-card stop on a 1-card hand; weaker if they have 2+ Elfnotes already.

interruption_points.timing: When Power Patron raises a Center monster's Level to Synchro Summon (the climb step)
interruption_points.action: Effect Veiler / Infinite Impermanence on the monster that wants to use its Center effect, or remove Power Patron before it becomes material so they lose the 'add 1 Elfnote' search and the climb.

interruption_points.timing: After 5+ total summons in one turn (this deck spams Synchro materials and SS's the girls)
interruption_points.action: Nibiru, the Primal Being. Elfnote routinely crosses 5 summons, so Nibiru is a premier stop unless they run the Fiendsmith/Caesar variant that protects against it.

interruption_points.timing: On any Synchro Summon / from-deck effect during the chain
interruption_points.action: Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit on a key Synchro or on Welcome Home/Rhapsodia as it's placed; Ghost Belle if they try GY recursion.

hand_traps.why: Deck reliably makes 5+ summons climbing into Synchros; tributes the whole board and leaves a Token for you. Best single hand trap vs pure builds.
hand_traps.when: Hold until they pass 5 summons, ideally right before the final boss Synchro.

hand_traps.why: Punishes the long Synchro chain hard. Lines around it exist but mostly become 2-card combos and still give you draws; in MD it forces a minimal board or a stop.
hand_traps.when: Activate at the very first special summon of their combo.

hand_traps.why: This deck searches repeatedly (Lucina, Power Patron-as-material, Tinia/Fortuna placing cards). Droll after their first search shuts off all further adds and cripples the climb.
hand_traps.when: Chain to the first search/add-to-hand, then they cannot search again.

hand_traps.why: Negates the key search (Lucina / Power Patron 'add 1 Elfnote' / deck-placement). Note: the deck is built to grind through lone Ash, so it is a tempo tax more than a hard stop on a developed hand.
hand_traps.when: On the FIRST search, especially Lucina or Power Patron's material add, on a thin hand.

hand_traps.why: Negates a girl's Center-MMZ effect or Power Patron mid-climb. Like Ash, single copies can be played through, so aim at the irreplaceable link in the chain.
hand_traps.when: Imperm before they commit; Veiler on the monster about to use its OPT engine effect.

hand_traps.why: Destroys a freshly placed Welcome Home / Rhapsodia or a Synchro mid-combo, breaking the Center-zone protection package.
hand_traps.when: When the Continuous Spell/Trap resolves onto the field, or on a key Synchro Summon.

board_breakers.why: Welcome Home only stops DESTRUCTION; Droplet sends/negates by other means, so it neuters Baronne/Crystal Wing and the Center monster without triggering destruction immunity.
Tribute-based removal ignores Welcome Home's destruction protection and clears the Center boss Synchro, also bypassing Rhapsodia's attack-redirect lock.
Going second their grindy multi-card board folds to Evenly; they keep only one card, blanking the Center-zone engine and negate pile.

Wipes the Continuous Spell+Trap (Welcome Home / Rhapsodia) that power the lock and S/T negate. Lightning Storm also clears their Synchros in ATK; bait the Rhapsodia S/T negate first if they have 3+ Elfnotes.
Their boards are full of generic-attribute Synchros (LIGHT/DARK) and the girls; SS dodges negates entirely and removes their boss monster as fusion material.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going first vs Elfnote: their interaction is fast Quick-effect Synchros plus the Center-zone protection, so do not just out-grind them; deploy your own negates and respect Rhapsodia's spell/trap negate (live once they hold 3+ Elfnotes). Going second: they are a weak going-second engine themselves, so the matchup swings on board breakers. Welcome Home blocks destruction on the Center monster, so prioritize non-destruction outs (Droplet, Kaijus, Super Poly, Evenly) over Raigeki-style removal; clear the S/T (Duster/Lightning Storm) to disable the negate and lock, then push. Open the turn with a hand trap to keep their board small enough that one breaker is enough.
counters.beginner_explanation: Recognize Elfnote by the three Singer girls (Lucina, Tinia, Fortuna) jumping to the middle monster zone and by Power Patron making Synchro monsters. The whole deck is a search-and-Synchro chain, so two things stop it: (1) a hand trap on the FIRST search or the FIRST summon, and (2) Nibiru once they have summoned five monsters in a turn. If they already have a board, do not try to destroy the middle monster, it is protected from destruction. Instead use cards that send, banish, or tribute it (Forbidden Droplet, a Kaiju, Super Polymerization) and blow up their face-up Spell and Trap with Harpie's Feather Duster or Lightning Storm to turn off their negate. When going second, lead with a hand trap so their board stays small, then one board breaker is usually enough.

counters.archetype: Spell-based control / grind deck (monsterless or near-monsterless backrow control)
counters.game_plan: Sky Striker keeps an empty Main Monster Zone (most effects only work with 0 monsters in your zone) and grinds card advantage through Spells, mainly Engage, which has NO once-per-turn limit and draws + searches every time you have 3+ Spells in grave. It floods the backrow with Quick-Play Mecha (Widow Anchor steals/negates, Shark Cannon banishes, Eagle Booster protects) behind Shizuku and Multirole, then wins slowly by out-resourcing you and answering threats one at a time. It is reactive, not explosive: it does not OTK, it strangles you over many turns.

key_cards.role: Engine heart. Searches any Sky Striker card AND draws when 3+ Spells in grave. NO once-per-turn limit, so it is recurred and re-activated all game. Cutting off Engage starves the deck.

Main starter monster. Tributes itself during opponent's turn or via Engage-fueled plays to bring out the Ace Link/Xyz that matters (Kagari to recur Spells, Hayate to send, Shizuku for the end board, Zero for protection).
Summoned off Raye; adds a Sky Striker Spell AND makes your key Spells unchainable for the turn. This is what walls hand traps and Called By once it resolves.
Link-1 that recurs a Sky Striker Spell (usually Engage or Linkage) from grave to hand. The primary advantage-loop piece.
End-board centerpiece: locks in a set Spell via Multirole and refills hand. Sits over 4-5 set Mecha as the control wall.
Quick-Play interaction: negates an opponent monster effect and steals the monster while you control 0 monsters. The main turn-disruption Mecha in their backrow.
Field/Continuous engine that sets a Sky Striker Spell from grave each turn and protects their Spells/Traps. Backbone of the grind plan.

interruption_points.timing: Their FIRST Engage activation (before 3 Spells are in grave, or the very first search)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the Engage search OR drop Droll & Lock Bird right after their first search. Droll is the strongest because it shuts off ALL further adds/searches for the turn, killing the unlimited Engage loop.

interruption_points.timing: On Sky Striker Ace = Zero's add/protection effect
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom or Ghost Belle the Zero search. Zero is the card that makes their Spells unchainable, so negating it keeps your disruption (and later board breakers) live.

interruption_points.timing: When Raye/Engage tries to Special Summon an Ace (Kagari/Shizuku/Hayate) in your zone or theirs
interruption_points.action: Effect Veiler / Infinite Impermanence on the summoned Ace, or Imperm on Raye, denies the recursion/search step and stops the link climb.

interruption_points.timing: End Phase Shizuku + Multirole set/add sequence
interruption_points.action: Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit on Multirole (Continuous) or Shizuku to break the end-board engine before it sets the backrow back up.

interruption_points.timing: During their grind turns when they re-activate recurred Engage
interruption_points.action: A second copy of Ash or a well-timed Droll mid-turn still cuts the loop, since Engage has no OPT and they lean on repeating it.

hand_traps.why: The single best hand trap vs Sky Striker (their 'kryptonite'). After their first add/search, Droll stops every further search AND draw for the turn, neutering the unlimited Engage engine that the whole deck runs on.
hand_traps.when: Drop it immediately after their FIRST search of the turn (usually the first Engage), not before. Holding for the first add maximizes lock value.

hand_traps.why: Negates an Engage search or the Zero add. Hits the deck where it lives. Slightly weaker than Droll because they can recur Engage and search again later, but it is the cleanest stop on a key add.
hand_traps.when: On the FIRST Engage (the add) when going second to slow setup, or on Zero's search to keep your disruption live. Be aware Crossout Designator / Called By can answer it.

hand_traps.why: Negates a key Ace on summon (Shizuku/Kagari) or Raye, and the column-lock can disrupt their backrow placement. Good because it works through their low monster count and sets up your own turn.
hand_traps.when: On the summoned Ace that matters, or set turn 1 to threaten their turn-2 plays. Strong going first to pre-load interaction.

hand_traps.why: Destroys Multirole or a key Ace (Zero/Shizuku), breaking the Continuous-card grind engine that rebuilds their backrow each turn.
hand_traps.when: On Multirole when it tries to set/protect, or on Zero/Shizuku on summon. Sky Striker is noted as especially vulnerable to Ogre.

hand_traps.why: Negates a key Ace effect (Kagari recursion, Shizuku) on your opponent's turn without using a board slot. Cheap, surgical disruption of the link loop.
hand_traps.when: On Kagari's recur or Shizuku's effect during their turn. Less impactful than Ash/Droll on the Spell engine itself.

hand_traps.why: Generally WEAK here. Sky Striker rarely summons 5+ monsters in a turn (they keep zones empty), so Nibiru usually never turns on. Do not rely on it.
hand_traps.when: Almost never live vs pure Sky Striker. Only relevant vs hybrid builds that combo. Side it out for this matchup.

hand_traps.why: Mediocre here (and banned in TCG). Sky Striker special summons very little (mostly one Ace per turn), so Maxx C draws you few cards and they can grind through. Useful mainly in Master Duel as a soft deterrent, not a real stop.
hand_traps.when: Master Duel only, turn-1 reactive. Expect low yield. They can play around it by minimizing summons.

board_breakers.why: One activation wipes their entire set backrow (the Mecha behind Shizuku). Their whole turn-1 plan is set cards, so a single board-wipe Spell erases the game plan. Top counter when going second.

Going second into their wide backrow, it banishes their cards FACE-DOWN, so the Mecha and Multirole are gone for the rest of the duel (cannot be recovered). Excellent because it punishes a full backrow and you are the one with the empty/behind field.

board_breakers.card: Cosmic Cyclone / Twin Twisters / Spell-Trap removal
board_breakers.why: Surgically banish Multirole or a threatening Widow Anchor before it resolves. Cosmic banishing is best because it dodges grave recursion the deck relies on.
Tribute away their Shizuku/Ace to clear the board centerpiece and put a beater down, ignoring their monster-based protection. Useful since their Aces are tough to run over normally.

Negates their set/active Spell-Trap Mecha (and any Ace) en masse during the turn, opening a lethal swing. Strong proactive break that also dodges Widow Anchor since you control monsters anyway by then.
Note: Sky Striker can play AROUND or under some floodgates by keeping 0 monsters; verify the specific floodgate works before siding it. Prefer hard removal over floodgates here.

counters.going_first_vs_second: GOING FIRST: Sky Striker is reactive, so going first you set your OWN disruption (Imperm, set traps) and develop a board they must answer one card at a time, then hold Droll/Ash for their turn-2 Engage. Do not over-extend into Widow Anchor (it steals/negates while they have 0 monsters) - bait it with a non-key monster first. GOING SECOND: This is where Sky Striker is most fragile. They will have a set backrow + Shizuku, so bring board breakers (Feather Duster/Lightning Storm/Evenly Matched) to wipe the Mecha, then push. Lead with the breaker BEFORE summoning so Widow Anchor has no monster to steal, then commit. Overall the deck is harder to beat in grind games than in a fast race, so close it out quickly once you break the board.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Sky Striker as a slow strangler, not a one-turn killer. It keeps its monster zone empty on purpose and rebuilds a wall of face-down Spell cards every turn, drawing extra cards off Engage (a card with NO once-per-turn limit) until it out-resources you. Two simple plans: (1) Going second, run a board-wipe Spell like Harpie's Feather Duster or Lightning Storm to blow up all their set cards at once, but cast it BEFORE you summon a monster so their Widow Anchor cannot steal it. (2) Hold Droll & Lock Bird (or Ash Blossom) and use it right after their first search of the turn to shut off their card-drawing engine. Skip Nibiru and mostly skip Maxx C against this deck - they barely summon, so those rarely do anything. Win fast once you break the board; do not let it grind.

counters.archetype: Reptile-based Ritual archetype (Earthbound Japanese-myth swords). NOTE: deck was labeled "Ritual/Warrior" in the request, but the core Mitsurugi monsters are EARTH Reptiles, not Warriors. Confidence on type: high.
counters.tier: Tier 2 (rogue-to-solid-meta in TCG as of June 2026; competitive but not top-of-format)
counters.game_plan: Mitsurugi is a Ritual recursion engine: it Ritual Summons Level 8 "Mitsurugi" monsters, then Tributes them for MORE Ritual Summons, and each Tribute triggers a graveyard effect that searches another Mitsurugi card AND revives the monster. Off one starter it snowballs into multiple Level 8s and Level 4s, then converts them into Xyz negates (Number 38 Titanic Galaxy, Number 90 Photon Lord) plus in-theme floodgate/destruction (Ame no Murakumo wipes your monsters on summon). The goal is a multi-interruption board that also keeps grinding back through GY recursion if you do break it.

key_cards.role: Best single-card starter. From hand it Special Summons a Mitsurugi from Deck (e.g. Saji), then Tributes it to trigger searches; chains the whole ritual loop. Recognize this and you know the combo is live.
Signature Ritual Spell. Can Ritual Summon from the DECK using hand/field material, AND Ritual Summon from the HAND using DECK material, each once per turn. Doubles ritual access and consistency.

key_cards.card: Mitsurugi no Mikoto, Saji / Aramasa / Kusanagi
key_cards.role: Level 4 engine pieces. Saji searches a Mitsurugi Spell/Trap on summon or tribute; Aramasa searches a Mitsurugi monster; Kusanagi recycles from GY/banish. These are the search effects that fuel the loop, and Aramasa is the usual Normal Summon.

Primary disruption boss. On Special Summon, destroys ALL monsters the opponent controls (once per turn, works no matter how it is summoned), plus a negate-or-discard effect. This is the card that punishes you for committing a board.
Defensive boss. Swarms/revives Reptiles from GY whenever the opponent Special Summons, making the board hard to out by going wide.
Extender/searchers that find Habakiri + the Ritual Spell and convert single pieces into the full line. Prayers is the consistency glue (and a known banlist target).

interruption_points.timing: On the Habakiri / Pre-Prep / Prayers SEARCH activation (the very first search of the turn)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring the search to deny the starter. Hitting the FIRST searcher (Pre-Prep, Prayers, or a Saji/Aramasa search) chokes the whole loop before it builds material.

interruption_points.timing: On the Special Summon from Deck (Habakiri summoning Saji from Deck)
interruption_points.action: Ghost Ogre, Effect Veiler or Infinite Impermanence the summoned/searching monster to stop its on-summon or tribute search and break the chain early.

interruption_points.timing: After they have made about 5 Special Summons in one chain/turn
interruption_points.action: Nibiru, the Primal Being. The loop pumps out multiple Level 8s and 4s, so the 5th+ summon is common BEFORE they finish. Hold Nibiru for the moment before they Xyz into negates. NOTE: good players run D/D/D Wave High King Caesar as Nibiru insulation, so it is not guaranteed.

interruption_points.timing: On the FIRST search effect of the turn, then locked all turn
interruption_points.action: Droll & Lock Bird. This is the single best hand trap vs Mitsurugi: after any card is added from Deck, no more cards can be added from Deck for the rest of the turn, which turns OFF the entire Habakiri/Saji/Aramasa/Murakumo search engine. Drop it as soon as they add the first card.

interruption_points.timing: On the Ritual Summon itself (mid-combo)
interruption_points.action: Dimensional Barrier (Ritual declaration) shuts off further ritual plays. Also Bystial Magnamhut / The Winged Dragon banishes their LIGHT/DARK or in-GY ritual monsters to deny the revive/recursion (note most Mitsurugi are EARTH, so Bystial targets are limited; primarily for splashed targets).

hand_traps.why: THE premier counter. Mitsurugi is built entirely on adding cards from Deck (search after search). After their first add, Droll stops all further adds-from-Deck for the turn, gutting the search-and-recur engine and leaving them with a fraction of the board.
hand_traps.when: The instant they resolve their FIRST search/add this turn (after Pre-Prep, Prayers, or the first Saji/Aramasa/Habakiri add). Do not wait.

hand_traps.why: Negates the key searcher/Special-Summon-from-Deck effect. Strong but single-target, so they can play around it with a second searcher; still denies a clean start.
hand_traps.when: On Pre-Preparation of Rites, Mitsurugi Prayers, or Habakiri's add/summon-from-Deck (the first one that matters).

hand_traps.why: The combo makes 5+ Special Summons easily, so Nibiru tributes the board for a 11/11 token. Caveat: skilled lists run D/D/D Wave High King Caesar specifically to dodge it, so check before assuming it lands.
hand_traps.when: After their 5th Special Summon, ideally right before they Xyz into their negates.

hand_traps.why: Punishes the heavy Special-Summon recursion (multiple ritual summons + revives). Either they draw you into a winning hand or they stop short of a full board. Format-dependent (legal in TCG, banned in Master Duel).
hand_traps.when: Main Phase 1, before they begin the loop. Force them to commit or stop.

hand_traps.why: Negates a key on-field effect (e.g. the searching/Special-Summoning monster) and, if set, the column-off bonus disrupts spells. Flexible interaction that can stop a pivotal trigger.
hand_traps.when: On the resolution of Habakiri's or a Mikoto's effect; or set going first to also catch Mitsurugi Ritual.

hand_traps.card: Effect Veiler / Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit
hand_traps.why: Veiler negates a Mikoto/Habakiri effect on field; Ghost Ogre destroys the monster trying to use its effect, stopping the search/revive. Both cut a link out of the chain.
hand_traps.when: Veiler on the monster's effect activation; Ghost Ogre when the engine monster tries to resolve its on-field search/summon.

hand_traps.why: Stops GY-revive / GY-search recursion (Mitsurugi's whole grind plan is GY-based). Niche but blanks the recursion turn.
hand_traps.when: On a GY-effect activation (a tributed Mitsurugi reviving itself or a GY recycle).

board_breakers.why: Best go-second out vs Mitsurugi. Their end board is multiple monsters (Murakumo, Futsu no Mitama, Xyz negates); Evenly forces them to banish down to one face-up card, collapsing the negate wall. Strong because it ignores targeting/negation.

If they end on attack-position monsters (Murakumo / Xyz bosses), Lightning Storm wipes all their monsters. Watch for set backrow that flips it to the spell/trap mode; still a clean reset going second.

Sends from hand/field to negate the effects AND halve ATK of multiple monsters at once, neutering Murakumo and the Xyz negates so you can push. Plays through most of their interruption since cost-paying chains awkwardly for them.
Tribute away their key boss (Murakumo or the negate Xyz) ignoring negation, since it is a tribute-summon, not a targeting destruction. Gets through Futsu no Mitama walls by removing the linchpin.
Wipes their backrow if the build leans on set traps (e.g. Mitsurugi Great Purification / floodgates). Less relevant vs pure monster boards, more vs trap-heavy/stun variants.

Fuses away their monsters (e.g. into Mudragon or Garura) ignoring negation. Excellent because it removes interruption material without giving them a trigger, though chainable timing matters vs their revive effects.

Raigeki destroys all their monsters (clean board wipe). Dark Ruler No More negates all their monster effects for the turn so the negates/destruction cannot fire, letting you swing through. DRNM is especially good since it shuts off Murakumo and Xyz negates at once.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Mitsurugi WANTS to go first to set up its multi-negate + Murakumo destruction board, then grind with GY recursion. Going FIRST against them: lead with disruption that pre-empts their turn (Droll/Ash in hand, or Imperm/Maxx C), and consider going first yourself with your own established board plus held interaction, because their turn-1 board is hard to break clean. Going SECOND against them: you NEED a board breaker (Evenly Matched, Droplet, DRNM, Lightning Storm) PLUS a way through the recursion. Lead breakers that ignore negation (Evenly, Droplet, Kaiju, Super Poly) because targeted destruction gets eaten by negates and revive triggers. Crucial: their GY engine means a single breaker often is not enough; chain a board wipe THEN a follow-up push, and use Droll/Ghost Belle to stop them rebuilding. If on the play, the highest-value single card is Droll & Lock Bird drawn for their turn.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Mitsurugi as a deck that recycles its own swords: every time it sacrifices a monster, it searches a new card AND brings the sacrificed one back, so it never runs out of gas. The simplest plan as a newbie: (1) If you have Droll & Lock Bird, drop it the moment they search the FIRST card off their starter (Pre-Prep, Prayers, or Habakiri). That one card shuts the whole engine down for the turn. (2) If you do not have a hand trap and they finish their board, do NOT use single-target removal (it gets negated). Instead use a board breaker that ignores negation, like Evenly Matched (going second) or Forbidden Droplet, to clear the wall, then push for game in the same turn. (3) Always assume they can grind back from the graveyard, so try to win the turn you break their board rather than trading one-for-one. Watch for the monster that destroys all your monsters when it is summoned (Ame no Murakumo), do not over-commit into it.

counters.archetype: Maliss (Alice in Wonderland-themed Cyberse/DARK banish-Link combo deck)
counters.game_plan: Maliss is a DARK Cyberse banish-loop combo deck. Every monster has an effect that triggers BY being banished and then Special Summons itself back from banishment, so they chain Dormouse / White Rabbit / Mad Hatter together to Link-climb into a wall of Link-3 "Q" bosses. They end on a resource loop (notably Q White Binder + the trap Maliss C GWC-06) that re-banishes and re-summons every turn, plus Q Hearts Crypter's un-negatable removal, making the board grindy and hard to fully clear.

key_cards.role: Best one-card starter. Banishes itself/another Maliss to begin the banish-summon loop. Recognize it as the combo ignition.
Second main starter. Can start the core combo alone; banishes to re-summon and extend.
Field Spell and one-card combo enabler. Banishes Dormouse/White Rabbit to Special Summon them from banishment, fueling the engine.
Key end-board Link. Sets a Maliss trap from deck/GY and banishes up to 3 cards from GYs on the opponent's turn, anchoring the resource loop.
Their most annoying trap. With all Maliss names in GY, it powers the loop and lets White Binder combo on your turn.
Strongest Link boss (needs exactly 3 monsters incl. a Maliss). If pointing to a monster, its removal CANNOT be negated.
Revival/utility Link; searches a Maliss Spell and swaps opponent ATK/DEF. Its revival effect is a prime Nibiru window.
Extender + hand trap. Banishes a LIGHT/DARK monster (Maliss are DARK) to summon itself AND banish a Maliss to trigger its on-banish effect. Double duty.

interruption_points.timing: On the FIRST Maliss banish-and-resummon (Dormouse / White Rabbit / Maliss in Underground activation)
interruption_points.action: This is the cleanest choke. Ash Blossom the search/summon effect, or fire Artifact Lancea here to lock all banishing for the turn. Hitting the very first banish stops the whole loop from forming.

interruption_points.timing: When the first Maliss monster's effect tries to add/search from deck
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring negates it. Earlier is better; once they have 2+ bodies they extend through one negate.

interruption_points.timing: When a Maliss monster is on field about to be used as Link material / activates on-field
interruption_points.action: Infinite Impermanence or Effect Veiler the active monster to break the chain before they Link-climb.

interruption_points.timing: After they Special Summon their 5th monster in one chain
interruption_points.action: Nibiru, the Primal Being tributes the board. Best deployed if they over-extend; many Maliss hands cannot rebuild through it without a live trap.

interruption_points.timing: On Maliss Q Red Ransom's revival effect resolving
interruption_points.action: Nibiru / a negate here is a strong specific window per meta consensus, but confirm they have no live trap to restart first.

interruption_points.timing: During the long extension chain (many Special Summons)
interruption_points.action: Maxx C forces them to either give massive card advantage or stop short. Maliss combos are far less flexible around Maxx C than around Droll.

hand_traps.why: THE standout counter. Quick effect, only cost is the discard so Ash can't stop it, locks ALL banishing for the turn. Maliss's entire engine is banish-and-return, so this brick-walls the combo.
hand_traps.when: Activate the moment they make their first banish (Dormouse/White Rabbit/Field Spell). Can also be held to disrupt their turn-end loop. Going first or second.

hand_traps.why: Maliss combos are far less flexible around Maxx C than Snake-Eyes; it either taxes them out of the full combo or hands you a fat draw. Strongest single generic vs this deck.
hand_traps.when: Activate in Main Phase 1 before they start summoning. They cannot easily Droll-loop out of it cleanly.

hand_traps.why: Negates the first search/summon-from-deck effect. Stops a fragile one-card hand cold.
hand_traps.when: On the FIRST Maliss search/special-summon effect. Diminishing value once they have multiple bodies in play.

hand_traps.why: Wipes the board after over-extension. Effective vs greedy Maliss hands; meta flags Red Ransom's revival as a good window.
hand_traps.when: After their 5th Special Summon, ideally on/after Red Ransom revival. Verify they lack a live trap to restart the loop first.

hand_traps.why: Negates a key active Maliss monster mid-combo and (if set) cuts their backrow Spell zone too. Good going second.
hand_traps.when: On the on-field Maliss monster about to be used as material, before the Link-climb resolves.

hand_traps.why: Negates the in-hand-cost-free active monster to break the chain. Weaker than Imperm/Ash but live vs the loop pieces.
hand_traps.when: On a key Maliss monster's field effect during the extension chain.

hand_traps.why: Honest assessment: WEAKER here. Players believe Maliss plays through Droll well enough; it is 'better to be Droll'd than Maxx-C'd.' Don't rely on it as your main answer.
hand_traps.when: Only as a backup after they've already searched once; deprioritize vs Lancea/Maxx C.

hand_traps.why: Shuts off Maliss in Underground (Field), the GWC-06 trap, and Q White Binder, gutting the resource loop even if it doesn't stop the initial combo.
hand_traps.when: Use to suffocate the grind/loop pieces rather than the opening; great in the matchup vs their end-board recursion.

board_breakers.why: Continuous trap that stops ALL banishing permanently. Since Maliss lives on banish-and-return, this is a near-hard-lock. Best set going first; weak to S/T removal.
Mass-negates their Link bosses' effects (incl. dodging some by chaining), letting you push through Hearts Crypter and White Binder. Strong going second.
Clears their attack-position Link bosses if you go second into an open board. Note: weaker if they have set traps (GWC-06) and good face-up disruption.
Going second into their multi-Link board, force them to one card. Excellent vs the wide Link-3 wall Maliss ends on.
Wipes their backrow, removing Maliss C GWC-06 and any set traps that fuel/restart the loop before you commit.
Floodgate monster preventing opponent banishing after a Special Summon. Caution: vulnerable to Triple Tactics Talent steal that lets them continue.
Continuous trap stopping banished/GY monsters from activating effects. Hits the return triggers, though it does NOT stop banishing-for-cost, so less complete than Iron Wall/Lancea.
Tribute away a key Link boss (e.g. Hearts Crypter) to open a lane, since their bosses don't appreciate being tributed off and removal-immunity doesn't save them.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going FIRST against them is about prevention: lead with a turn-1 floodgate-style answer in hand. Set Imperial Iron Wall or hold Artifact Lancea/Maxx C; these stop the engine before it forms and are far better than trying to out-grind their loop. Going SECOND you need to break an established wall: open with Harpie's Feather Duster (clear GWC-06/backrow) then Lightning Storm/Evenly Matched/Forbidden Droplet, or Kaiju a key boss. Remember Hearts Crypter's removal can't be negated when it points to a monster, and they keep a turn-loop of disruption, so single-target interaction is rarely enough.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Maliss as a deck that wins by BANISHING its own monsters and bringing them right back, over and over, climbing into a row of boss monsters. The whole deck is one big banish loop. So the #1 newbie rule: stop the banishing. The single best card is Artifact Lancea (drop it the moment they banish anything; it shuts off all banishing for the turn and Ash can't stop it). Maxx C is your other go-to, used before they start comboing. If you go second and they already have a board, blow up their face-down traps with Harpie's Feather Duster first, then sweep their monsters with Lightning Storm or Evenly Matched. Don't lean on Droll here; it's much weaker against this deck than against most.

counters.archetype: K9 (Beast / mixed-Type FIRE-Beast core engine; actual cards span Warrior, Beast-Warrior, Aqua, Pyro across EARTH/DARK/WIND/LIGHT)
counters.game_plan: K9 is a Level-5-centric combo/control engine that floods Rank 5 XYZ plays, often on the OPPONENT's turn. It chains its own "hand-trap-like" monsters (Izuna, Lupis) that self-Special-Summon when you activate a monster effect from hand or GY, then makes K9-17 "Ripper" (Rank 5) to negate your follow-up hand traps and Nibiru. The end goal is a board with a hand/GY negate (Ripper), banish/disruption pieces (Werewolf, Hound), and in hybrid builds a Mitsurugi field-nuke or Vanquish Soul / Crystron payload.

key_cards.role: Main starter/extender. Special Summons itself + a Level 5 from hand, then searches a K9 (usually Izuna). The card that gets the combo rolling, fuels Rank 5s, and digs.

Rank 5 XYZ, the linchpin. Quick Effect: detach 1 to NEGATE a monster effect activated in the hand or GY. This shuts off your post-Ripper hand traps AND Nibiru. Stopping Ripper from hitting the board is the whole game.
Searchable Level 5 'baited' piece. Self-SS when opponent activates a monster effect from hand/GY, sends a K9 to GY. Provides bodies for Rank 5 (Ripper) reactively.
Level 5 enabler. Self-SS under the same trigger as Izuna, plus a quick effect to XYZ Summon (even on opponent's turn) — the engine that lets K9 make Ripper on YOUR turn off your own hand traps.

Spell engine: searches a K9 monster, gives +900 ATK whenever opponent used a hand/GY monster effect, and re-sets a K9 Quick-Play if destroyed. Consistency + grind glue. Stake your Soul! is the companion searcher.
End-board disruption. Werewolf (Rank 9) attacks multiple times and banishes from hand/field/GY; Hound (Rank 5) is destruction-immune and grows in ATK off opponent monster effects.

interruption_points.timing: On Jokul's Special Summon / its search (in response to the on-summon search trigger)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the search, OR Imperm/Veiler the Jokul body before it resolves. This is the single best window — Jokul is the main starter that builds the Level 5 board.

interruption_points.timing: BEFORE Ripper is XYZ Summoned (the pre-Ripper window)
interruption_points.action: This is the critical phase. Until Ripper is on board, your hand traps and Nibiru still resolve. Fire your strongest disruption here — do NOT save it. Every hand trap is dead once Ripper exists.

interruption_points.timing: When opponent self-SSes Izuna/Lupis off YOUR monster-effect hand trap
interruption_points.action: Recognize that activating a hand trap can FEED them (triggers Izuna/Lupis). If you only have one hand trap and they have the Lupis line, sometimes hold it rather than hand them a free Rank 5 / Ripper.

interruption_points.timing: On the 5th+ Summon during a single Main Phase (before Ripper)
interruption_points.action: Drop Nibiru, the Primal Being. K9 floods bodies fast and can hit 5 summons pre-Ripper, but you MUST land it before Ripper or it gets negated.

interruption_points.timing: During the opponent-turn XYZ window (Lupis quick-effect)
interruption_points.action: K9 often makes Ripper on the opponent's turn. If you are the turn player, expect interaction — bait the Lupis XYZ before committing your real play.

hand_traps.why: Stops the Jokul search and the A Case for K9 / Stake your Soul! searches — the consistency backbone. Also baiting their own Ash makes it harder for them to meet FIRE/Attribute requirements and removes a Stake target.
hand_traps.when: On the FIRST search you see (Jokul on-summon, A Case, or Stake your Soul!). Use it pre-Ripper.

hand_traps.why: K9 mass-summons Level 5s and can reach 5+ summons in one Main Phase. Tributes their board and gives them a small token — devastating IF it lands before Ripper.
hand_traps.when: The moment they hit 5 summons, BEFORE Ripper is made. Negated by Ripper, so never hold it past that point.

hand_traps.why: Non-monster-effect negate, so it does NOT trigger Izuna/Lupis (which key off monster effects from hand/GY) and dodges Ripper entirely. Best single hand trap vs K9; also column-locks their spells/traps.
hand_traps.when: On a key combo monster's effect (Jokul, Lupis, or whatever bridges to Ripper). Safe to use at any point — Ripper can't negate it.

hand_traps.why: Negates a combo monster on field without being a 'hand/GY monster effect that Ripper catches' once it resolves on a board monster; pairs with Imperm to find Nibiru timing. Stops Jokul/Lupis effects.
hand_traps.when: On the Jokul/Lupis effect during the build, before Ripper. Less ideal than Imperm if Ripper is already threatened.

hand_traps.why: K9 is search-heavy (Jokul searches, A Case, Stake your Soul!). Droll after their first search shuts off all further adding-to-hand and can brick the line.
hand_traps.when: Immediately AFTER their first search resolves, before they search again. Note: it activates from hand, so post-Ripper it gets negated — fire it early.

hand_traps.why: Destroys A Case for K9 / Stake your Soul! or an XYZ on summon. Flexible answer to the spell engine or to Ripper itself.
hand_traps.when: On A Case/Stake activation, or on Ripper when it summons (before it can detach). Activates from hand → negated post-Ripper, so use it on Ripper's summon at the latest.

hand_traps.why: Punishes K9's heavy special-summon volume — they SS many Level 5s and XYZ. Forces them to either over-extend into your draws or stop short of Ripper.
hand_traps.when: Open of their turn / on first Special Summon. They cannot negate the draw with Ripper (it's a card draw, not the monster effect Ripper catches), but in MD they'll often try to play through or stop.

board_breakers.why: K9 leans on backrow support (A Case for K9, Stake your Soul!, Quick-Plays) and presents ATK-position XYZ. Clears either monsters or spells/traps; the deck is described as horribly bad against board breakers and spell/trap removal.

Brutal vs their wide XYZ board going second — they keep one card, you wipe the rest including Ripper. Note some pilots cut their own copies because they prefer turn-2 disrupts, meaning yours hits harder.
Nukes their entire backrow (A Case, Stake your Soul!, set Quick-Plays) which is the grind/protection layer, opening Ripper and the field for an OTK.
Negates Ripper and the disruption XYZ (Werewolf/Hound) at once. Going second this neuters the negate board so your follow-up resolves. Strong but pilots debate its impact vs pure disruption.
Turns off Ripper's negate and the rest of the monster-effect board for your turn, letting you push through. Cheap, no cost to your board, ideal going second to OTK past a Ripper wall.
Tribute away Ripper or a problem XYZ regardless of its protection (Hound is destruction-immune but not tribute-immune). Single-card answer to the key negate, then swing/OTK.

Situational — only clean if their on-board monsters match a generic Fusion's materials (K9 Types/Attributes are mixed: Warrior/Beast-Warrior/EARTH/WIND/LIGHT, NOT uniformly FIRE Beast), so verify targets. Uncounterable removal when it lines up.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going FIRST against you (you're the K9 player's opponent on turn 2): expect a Ripper hand/GY negate plus banish/disruption (Werewolf/Hound) and possibly a Mitsurugi field-nuke in hybrid builds — lead with board breakers (Lightning Storm, Evenly Matched, Duster, Dark Ruler No More, Kaiju) BEFORE committing, then push. Going SECOND for you / when YOU build first: hold up disruption for their opponent-turn XYZ window (they make Ripper on your turn via Lupis); set Imperm (it dodges Ripper and Izuna/Lupis triggers) and don't over-commit into a Lupis quick-effect XYZ. Golden rule both ways: stop Ripper before it resolves — every hand trap after it is dead. Imperm and Nibiru-before-the-5th-summon are your safest pre-Ripper interactions.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of K9 as a deck that builds a wall of one big negate — "Ripper" — that shuts off most hand traps you throw at it, and it can even build that wall on YOUR turn. So the whole fight is: stop Ripper from ever appearing. Use your hand traps EARLY (on their first Jokul or on their searches), don't save them, because once Ripper is up they stop working. Infinite Impermanence is your best friend — Ripper can't negate it and it doesn't accidentally feed their Izuna/Lupis. If you're going second and they already have a board, don't fight monster-for-monster; just blow it all up with cards like Lightning Storm, Harpie's Feather Duster, Dark Ruler No More, or bounce/tribute Ripper with a Kaiju, then attack. The deck is fragile to board wipes and backrow removal — that's its weak spot.

counters.game_plan: Reactive grind-and-control deck that plays on BOTH turns. Vanquish Soul monsters reveal EARTH/FIRE/DARK monsters in hand to fire Quick Effects (removal, steal, or advantage) on either player's turn, slowly out-resourcing you. The K9 engine bolts on Level 5 spam (Izuna, Lupis) to drop disruptive Xyz like K9-17 Ripper on your turn, including a monster-effect negate that protects the whole strategy. Wins by attrition: keep interruptions up, never run out of cards, fade your pushes.

key_cards.role: Engine starter/proc enabler. Quick Effect SS from hand by revealing a VS; on field steals opponent's lowest-ATK monster OR SS a VS from deck. Procs the K9 line if you have DARK+EARTH. Priority target to deny.
Main advantage generator + searcher with removal. Baits interruption: if they already hold Razen, it dodges your hand traps and rebuilds. Key card to recognize early.

Boss/finisher (Dragon). Quick Effect SS itself by bouncing another VS (dodges Veiler/Imperm). Can be made unaffected by opponent effects, OR non-target destroy any card by revealing one of each VS attribute, getting around protection.
THE problem card. Xyz dropped via K9-00 Lupis; has a monster-effect negate (usable from hand or GY). This is why monster hand traps are largely dead vs this deck.
K9 Level 5 spam payoff. Lupis enables dropping disruptive Xyz (Ripper) on your turn; Izuna is an interruption piece. Losing these cripples their turn-0 plan.
Consistency spell. Reveal a monster to SS a same-attribute VS from deck. Extends and helps proc effects. Ash-able search-equivalent.

interruption_points.timing: On a search effect (Razen, Stake Your Soul!, K9 searchers, Saryuja draw-search)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom to deny the search. Best when it cuts off access to a needed attribute (especially a FIRE monster) rather than just a body.

interruption_points.timing: When they tag-out / SS a Vanquish Soul via Quick Effect (Hollie Sue, Caesar, Heavy Borger)
interruption_points.action: Recognize that targeted negates (Veiler/Imperm) get dodged by the bounce-to-SS effects. Hold targeted interaction for a moment they CAN'T tag out.

interruption_points.timing: After they commit 4+ monsters to the field (K9 Level 5 spam overextension)
interruption_points.action: Nibiru the Primal Being. Best disruption in the matchup, especially after baiting/clearing Ripper. Strips both their board and gives you the token to push.

interruption_points.timing: During YOUR Standby Phase, before they can set up
interruption_points.action: Infinite Impermanence. VS Quick Effects and Ripper negate are tied to Main Phase windows, so Standby-phase Imperm slips past Ripper's window better than Veiler.

interruption_points.timing: On the first proc / first K9 special summon of the turn
interruption_points.action: If you must use a monster hand trap, force it onto the FIRST relevant effect to bait Ripper's negate before your real disruption lands.

hand_traps.why: Strongest interaction in the matchup. Punishes K9 Level 5 overextension, non-targeting so it ignores VS protection, removes Rock + monsters which is exactly the card advantage VS needs. Pairs with Veiler/Faimena to bait Ripper first, then resolve clean.
hand_traps.when: After they Normal/Special summon 5+ monsters in a turn (K9 spam). Ideally after Ripper's negate is spent.

hand_traps.why: Hits searches (Razen, Stake Your Soul!, K9 searchers, Saryuja). Extra value: baiting it out can deny their access to a FIRE attribute monster and removes a Stake target, choking future procs.
hand_traps.when: On the first impactful search, especially one that grabs a FIRE monster they need to proc effects.

hand_traps.why: The most reliable hand trap here. Can be activated during your Standby Phase, sidestepping VS Main-Phase Quick Effects and Ripper's negate window. Also turns off backrow if monster-zone column matches.
hand_traps.when: Standby Phase before their setup, or on a key monster they can't bounce away (can't tag out of it).

hand_traps.why: Slows the search-heavy engine, but limited: if Droll lands after Razen already searched, the VS player can still make Rock and set up on your turn. Decent but not a hard stop.
hand_traps.when: After the FIRST search of the turn, before they chain multiple searches.

hand_traps.why: Master Duel staple turn-0 tax. K9 spams Special Summons, so it draws a lot. But VS can play through it on a grind plan and they may have Droll/Ghost Belle back. Forces a decision, rarely a hard stop.
hand_traps.when: Turn 0 before they start, fastest possible window. Expect them to either stop short or feed you and grind back.

hand_traps.why: Usable but frequently dodged: Caesar Valius and Heavy Borger SS themselves by bouncing another VS, escaping targeted negation. Best as a Nibiru-enabler (bait Ripper, clear a body) rather than a standalone answer.
