hand_traps.when: To bait Ripper's negate before Nibiru, or on a monster that cannot tag out of it.

hand_traps.why: Can pop a continuous setup/Xyz material piece, but VS protection (Vanquish Soul Start!/Snow Devil) and Ripper limit value. Situational, not a primary answer.
hand_traps.when: On a field card you can hit before protection comes up.

board_breakers.why: Top-tier answer. Non-targeting negate-and-shrink that VS/K9 has no clean response to. Bypasses VS protection and Caesar's unaffected mode is the only dodge. Pushes through the layered board.
Excellent going second. The layered end board is full of monsters; Evenly forces them to one card, gutting the interruption shell. VS/K9 has essentially no answer to it.
Non-targeting banish-fusion that eats their monsters (including off-archetype/Dragon Caesar targets). Can't be responded to by most VS/K9 interruptions; strong board reset.

Reasonably effective: VS/K9 has no omni-negate or S/T negate, so backrow-clear usually resolves. Lightning Storm also clears their attack-position monster line going second. Caveat: monster-only destruction is blunted by VS protection cards.

Tribute away a protected/unaffected threat (gets around VS protection since it's a tribute, not destruction). Useful to remove Caesar Valius in unaffected mode, but check attribute interactions before relying on it.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going first: race to a board they can't out, because their end board with Ripper negate + VS Quick Effects is brutal to break. Bait Ripper's negate with a throwaway effect, then resolve your real play. Expect disruption ON your turn (Hollie Sue steal, Izuna, Lupis into Ripper), so play around it and don't overcommit into Nibiru-style punishes from THEM. Going second: hard-mulligan toward board breakers. Forbidden Droplet, Evenly Matched, and Super Polymerization are the cards that actually win the game; Nibiru after they overextend is the best hand trap. Save Evenly for the End Phase, lead with Droplet/Storm to crack protection, then push. Note: VS protection (Start!/Snow Devil) blunts pure destruction, so prioritize non-targeting/non-destruction breakers.
counters.beginner_explanation: This deck is annoying because it does stuff on YOUR turn too, and the K9 part (especially the Xyz monster called Ripper) shuts off your usual monster hand traps by negating them. So don't expect Effect Veiler or one Ash to win you the game. Two mental rules: (1) Their cards reveal EARTH/FIRE/DARK monsters in hand to work, so if you can deny them a FIRE monster (Ash on a search) you choke them. (2) Their board looks scary but it dies to non-destruction board breakers. If you're going second, hold Forbidden Droplet or Evenly Matched and you usually win; if they greedily flood the field with K9 monsters, Nibiru wipes it. Going first, just make a strong board, bait out Ripper with a small effect first, then do your real combo.

counters.game_plan: EARTH Rock combo deck that uses cheap one-card starters (Conduction Warrior Linear Magnum +/-) plus Magnet Bonding and an extra Normal Summon from Plasma Magnum to assemble Valkyrion + Berserkion and Fusion Summon Imperion Magnum the Superconductive Battlebot, a 4000/4000 omni-negate. It backs that up with extra interruptions (Naturia Beast, I:P + Apollousa-style follow-ups, Plasma Magnum) and is resilient because Imperion floats into Valkyrion + Berserkion when your removal kills it. The goal is a one-card omni-negate board that grinds and re-floats.

key_cards.card: Conduction Warrior Linear Magnum Plus Minus
key_cards.role: Main 1-card starter. Sends 2 Magnet Warriors from Deck to GY to Special Summon itself and snowball into the full combo. Recognize this resolving = combo is live.
Quick-Play engine glue. Returns Valkyrion + Berserkion from GY/banishment back to Deck so Imperion can be Fusion Summoned off basically nothing. The card that makes the Imperion finish consistent.

Fusion that searches a Magnet Spell/Trap on summon AND grants an extra Normal Summon, and can dump a Magna Warrior to Normal Summon a Magnet Warrior. Major extender that refuels and pushes through one disruption.

Boss / payoff. Lv10 4000/4000 Fusion (Valkyrion + Berserkion). Omni-negate once per turn during either turn (negate + destroy any S/T or monster effect). If removed by opponent, floats into Valkyrion + Berserkion from hand/Deck. Cannot be Special Summoned except by proper Fusion.

key_cards.card: Valkyrion the Magna Warrior / Berserkion the Electromagna Warrior
key_cards.role: Required Fusion materials for Imperion and recursion engines (Valkyrion revives Alpha/Beta/Gamma). These names tell you Imperion is the target.

key_cards.card: Sigma Plus / Sigma Minus / Epsilon / Duoterion
key_cards.role: Extenders and GY-fuel. Reveal/dump effects that rebuild materials and let the deck play through single hand traps like Droll and Ash.

interruption_points.timing: On the first Special Summon effect of Conduction Warrior Linear Magnum Plus Minus (it sending 2 Magnet Warriors from Deck to GY to summon itself)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the Deck-to-GY send, or Imperm/Veiler the summoned Linear Magnum, to deny the 1-card start before it fills the GY.

interruption_points.timing: On Magnet Bonding (Quick-Play) returning Valkyrion + Berserkion to the Deck
interruption_points.action: This is the lynchpin for the Imperion Fusion. Counter it (Ash if it adds/recurs, or just remove the materials) and the omni-negate often cannot come up.

interruption_points.timing: On Plasma Magmum's on-summon search of a Magnet Spell/Trap and its extra Normal Summon
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the search; Imperm/Veiler to shut off the extra Normal Summon / dump effect and cut the extension.

interruption_points.timing: When 5 monsters have hit the field during the combo (before the Imperion Fusion)
interruption_points.action: Nibiru, the Primal Being. This deck Special Summons many bodies fast, so the 5th summon usually arrives BEFORE Imperion is up and before it can negate Nibiru.

interruption_points.timing: On any Magnet Warrior search/add-to-hand or GY-recursion add (Linear add, Magna Warrior recur)
interruption_points.action: Droll & Lock Bird after their first search shuts off further adds. Note: they have a known line to grind through one Droll, so combine with another disruption.

interruption_points.timing: At the moment Imperion declares its omni-negate
interruption_points.action: Bait it with a low-value Spell/Trap or hand trap first, then resolve your real play. One Imperion = one negate per turn; the second threat resolves.

hand_traps.why: Best hand trap vs this deck. It mass-Special-Summons to reach 5 summons before Imperion is online, so Nibiru tributes the whole board and Imperion can't negate it. Community consensus: Magnet loses to Nibiru.
hand_traps.when: Hold until they have summoned 5 monsters in a turn (almost always before the Imperion Fusion), then activate.
On Linear Magnum's Deck-to-GY send, on Plasma Magnum's search, or on Magnet Bonding if it recurs/adds.
hand_traps.why: Hits the deck's GY-loading and search effects. Not a clean stop on its own (they build around single Ash), but denies a key add and slows the line.

hand_traps.when: On the first relevant monster effect (Linear Magnum, Plasma Magnum) and ideally set turn 1 to also stop your opponent and dodge Droll-style turn-skip cards.
hand_traps.why: Negates a key combo piece's effect; spell-negation on Imperm also helps vs their Quick-Play (Magnet Bonding) board after.

hand_traps.when: On Plasma Magnum or Linear Magnum during their main combo turn.
hand_traps.why: Shuts off the extension/extra Normal Summon. Cheaper than Imperm but no S/T coverage.

hand_traps.when: Immediately after their FIRST search/add (e.g., off Plasma Magnum or Duoterion).
hand_traps.why: Caps further adds-to-hand. Caveat: they have a documented line to grind through one Droll, so it is a soft-lock, not a hard stop, best paired with a second trap.

hand_traps.when: At the very start of their turn before they commit, or chain to their first Special Summon.
hand_traps.why: Punishes a deck that Special Summons many bodies. They draw you cards or get choked. Note: many builds run Droll/Called by the Grave to fight back, so value varies.

hand_traps.when: On a key on-field effect activation (e.g., a recurring material or a Fusion-piece's effect).
hand_traps.why: Flexible single-target out; decent but lower impact than Nibiru/Imperm against this deck.

board_breakers.why: Top out vs Magnet. Sends from hand/field as cost so it dodges Imperion's omni-negate read on the chain, halves Imperion's ATK and negates its effects, opening the board. Community consensus: Magnet loses to Droplet.
Cannot be responded to (no negating its activation), so Imperion's omni-negate does nothing. Fuse away Imperion or their EARTH Rock bodies for a clean removal that also nets you a body.

Tribute-summoning over Imperion does not trigger an activation Imperion can negate, removing the omni-negate. Note Imperion floats into Valkyrion + Berserkion if it leaves by your card effect, so pair with follow-up.
Going second into a face-up attack-position omni-negate board: nukes all their attack-position monsters at once. Best when they have no backrow and monsters are in ATK.
End of your battle phase going second, force them to banish down to one card. Strong because it ignores Imperion's negate (it banishes, and they choose) and dismantles a wide Magnet board.
Clears the Magnet Spell/Trap support (Magnet Bonding setups, searched S/T) if they leaned on backrow; lower priority since the threat is mostly the monster board.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going FIRST: you mostly do not face their board, so do not overcommit; set Infinite Impermanence and hold removal for when they go for Imperion. Going SECOND: you are racing a 4000/4000 omni-negate that re-floats. Prioritize NON-targeting, non-activatable outs that ignore the negate: Super Polymerization, Forbidden Droplet, Kaijus, Evenly Matched (post-battle), Lightning Storm. Spend a throwaway card to bait the single omni-negate, then resolve your real breaker. Remember Imperion floats into Valkyrion + Berserkion when YOUR card removes it, so plan a second push.
counters.beginner_explanation: This deck wants to spend one cheap card to build a 4000-ATK monster called Imperion Magnum that can negate ONE of your cards each turn, and it comes back if you kill it. Simplest plan: hold Nibiru and use it once they have summoned a bunch of monsters (around the 5th summon) and BEFORE Imperion is finished, that wipes the board. If you are going second into a finished board, do not use cards that 'activate' into Imperion (it will just negate them). Instead use cards it cannot stop: Super Polymerization, Forbidden Droplet, or a Kaiju to eat the big monster, then attack. If you have two threats, throw a weak one first to soak the one negate, then play your real one.

counters.archetype: Radiant Typhoon (WIND monster archetype built around Mystical Space Typhoon / Quick-Play Spell support and counter-Quick-Play)
counters.game_plan: Radiant Typhoon is a WIND combo/control deck that chains self-summoning WIND monsters (Swen, Eldom) into searches, fuels its graveyard with Mystical Space Typhoon (MST), then sets up a backrow-and-board of floating negations. Off one starter it builds a 3-disruption board (a Link monster like Veralun/Varuroon, a negating Continuous Trap like Ascendance/Mandate, plus an MST/Quick-Play it can chain to dodge interaction); off two cards it scales to 4-5 disruptions adding extra Links/Xyz and a monster-negate (Vibrant Vortex). Its signature payoff is bouncing the opponent's whole monster field to hand via Shiina as long as a WIND monster survives.

key_cards.role: Primary 1-card starter. Special Summons itself (if MST is in GY or opponent has no S/T) and searches the next piece (Chant/Eldom). Hit this or its search to deny the whole combo.
Second self-summoning starter/extender; on summon adds another Radiant Typhoon monster or MST. Half of the strongest 2-card combo (Eldom + Crosia).
The combo engine card. It searches two pieces (Ascendance + MST) and converts hands into full boards. THE #1 hand-trap target.
Quick-Play searcher that bridges starters into the chain; can be its own 1-card line (Chant -> Eldom).
Archetype enabler. Lives in GY to unlock free WIND Special Summons and is chained to their own cards mid-combo to build chain-link walls that dodge hand-trap negation.

key_cards.card: Radiant Typhoon Veralun / Varuroon, the Marine Eidolon
key_cards.role: Link payoff. Grabs a free MST, converts a problem opposing monster into a Continuous Spell, and fetches a Radiant Typhoon Continuous Trap straight to the field when a Quick-Play resolves.
Continuous Trap that provides the end-board negation/disruption and recycles archetype cards for advantage; the floating negation you must respect or remove.

key_cards.card: Shiina, Twin Tempests of Celestial Thunder
key_cards.role: Going-first finisher. Bounces the opponent's entire monster field to hand while a WIND monster is on board. Remove the WIND body and Shiina's bounce is neutered.
Generic Extra Deck interruption (banish/negate). Note: once it leaves the field they cannot recycle it, so banishing it is a clean hard answer.

interruption_points.timing: On Crosia (Krosea) resolving its search
interruption_points.action: This is the single highest-value stop. Crosia searches two pieces and is the load-bearing card of every multi-card combo. Negate or Ash its search and the board collapses to almost nothing.

interruption_points.timing: On the FIRST starter's summon/search (Swen or Eldom/Eldom)
interruption_points.action: If they open a single starter, denying its on-summon search breaks the 1-card line before it reaches Crosia. Imperm/Veiler the summoned body or Ash the search.

interruption_points.timing: On Chant's activation/search
interruption_points.action: Chant is a Quick-Play searcher that bridges into the chain. Ash Blossom on the Chant search (or Imperm if it pulls a monster effect) cuts a common entry point.

interruption_points.timing: Before they bury/chain MST
interruption_points.action: MST in GY is the engine. Droll & Lock Bird after their first search shuts off every subsequent add-to-hand for the turn, choking the combo mid-chain.

interruption_points.timing: On the Link/Xyz summon (Veralun/Varuroon or the Xyz 'Totem')
interruption_points.action: If the combo gets this far, Nibiru (if 5+ summons happened) or S:P Little Knight banishing a key body removes a disruption piece before the end board locks in. Beware they chain MST to build chain-link walls that dodge single negates here.

hand_traps.why: Best single answer. Negates Crosia's search (or Swen/Eldom/Chant search). Sources explicitly call Ash on Crosia the primary disruption.
hand_traps.when: On the first search you can hit, ideally Crosia. If they only open one starter, Ash the starter's search instead.

hand_traps.why: Negates the on-field effect of Crosia or a starter and (if set blind) also turns off a Spell/Trap column. Explicitly recommended on Crosia. Doubles as a board breaker going second.
hand_traps.when: On Crosia or the active starter's effect; set it pre-emptively going second to threaten their backrow column too.

hand_traps.why: After their first add-to-hand, Droll stops all further searching for the turn. Radiant Typhoon is search-chain dependent, so this strands the combo. Chain it once they pass priority / after the first search, not into the draw phase.
hand_traps.when: After the opponent's first search of the turn (after the chain resolves), to lock out every subsequent Crosia/Eldom/Veralun search.

hand_traps.why: Negates a single monster effect (the summoned Swen/Eldom or Crosia) without needing a Spell/Trap to be safe; a soft answer when you lack Ash. Listed as an effective interruption.
hand_traps.when: On the resolving monster effect of the starter or Crosia during the combo, ideally pre-Crosia.

hand_traps.why: The deck Special Summons several WIND monsters and Links to build its board, so Maxx C draws heavily and pressures them to stop short. Strong in Master Duel where it is legal.
hand_traps.when: Before they begin Special Summoning (in response to the first SS). Expect them to play around it; Called by / Crossout shuts it off.

hand_traps.why: Full combo lines pass through 5+ summons (multiple SS + Links/Xyz). Nibiru wipes the board and the token blocks Shiina's WIND-body requirement somewhat.
hand_traps.when: After their 5th summon of the turn, before they finish the Link/Xyz end board.

hand_traps.why: Flexible target: can destroy a key Continuous Spell/Trap (Ascendance/Mandate) or a problematic field card mid-combo. Soft pick if you lack Ash.
hand_traps.when: On the activation of their Continuous Trap/Spell, or a card that floats, to remove a disruption piece.

board_breakers.why: Going first into their established board: blow up their backrow (Ascendance/Mandate and any set Quick-Plays) if they have no face-up attack monster, or clear monsters if they have no backrow. Removes the floating-trap negation layer.
Wipes their entire Spell/Trap zone (the Continuous Trap disruption + set Quick-Plays/MST). Radiant Typhoon leans on backrow, so a one-sided backrow nuke is brutal. (TCG-legal; MD currently limited.)
Going second into a wide board, force them to banish down to one card. Excellent against their multi-piece (Link + Xyz + traps) end board built going first.
Negate and shrink multiple of their face-up disruption pieces (Veralun/Varuroon, Vibrant Vortex, Continuous Trap effects) at once; flexible quick-effect to push through negations.
Tribute away their key WIND body / boss (e.g. the Shiina or the Link payoff). Removing the WIND monster also disables Shiina's bounce, and Kaiju ignores their on-field protections by tributing.
Cannot be responded to, eats their monsters as Fusion material (great vs the Link/Xyz board), and bypasses their negations entirely. Strong tech if your Extra Deck supports it.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going first the deck wants to resolve its 1-to-3-card combo and pass with a Link (Veralun/Varuroon), a negating Continuous Trap (Ascendance/Mandate), and an MST/Quick-Play in hand to chain for protection; if uninterrupted off two cards it reaches 4-5 disruptions plus a monster-negate (Vibrant Vortex). As the opponent going SECOND vs that board: bring board breakers (Lightning Storm / Feather Duster / Evenly / Droplet) to clear the trap layer, and remove the WIND body to shut off Shiina. When YOU go first against Radiant Typhoon they will play more reactively (going second they fan out searches and use Quick-Effect chains to dodge single hand traps), so hold disruption for their Crosia and watch for them chaining MST to build chain-link walls that sidestep one negate. Sided board breakers matter more than extra hand traps because their floating Continuous Traps survive a single point of interaction.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of this deck as a search engine that runs on Mystical Space Typhoon. They summon a WIND monster for free, search the next piece, and the chain snowballs into a board of traps that negate you. The one card that matters most is Crosia (sometimes spelled Krosea): it searches two cards and powers the whole thing. So the simple rule for a newbie is: hold your Ash Blossom or Infinite Impermanence and use it on Crosia. If they only have a small opening, hit the very first search instead. If they already built a board, don't try to out-negate them, just blow up their back row with Lightning Storm or Harpie's Feather Duster and bounce/tribute away their WIND monster so their big Shiina bounce stops working. Watch out for them chaining their own MST mid-combo, that is a trick to make one hand trap miss, so when in doubt save your interruption for Crosia.

counters.game_plan: Yummy is a Synchro combo deck that turns a single Link-1 monster into a wall of Level 2 "Yummy Way" Synchros. It searches and special-summons its small Yummy monsters from hand off a Link-1, makes Yummy Way Synchros that load up resources, then climbs into a generic Synchro end board (omni-negates) plus its field spells. On the opponent's turn the Yummy Ways and field spell Acroquey "tag out" by bouncing themselves to the Extra Deck and reviving Yummy monsters from the GY with built-in disruption (face-downs, destruction), so the board re-forms even after you push through it.

key_cards.role: The starters. Each special summons itself from hand if you control a Link-1 or Level 2 Synchro, then searches/draws. Cupsy's add becomes a generic DRAW when summoned by a Synchro effect, dodging Ash/Droll on extensions.

The engine core. Can be Synchro Summoned using a Link-1 in place of a tuner, are themselves Tuners, and TAG OUT on opponent effects (return to ED, revive 2 Yummy from GY with disruption). This is the loop that re-forms the board.
Searches the Yummy Field Spell. This is a 'no-Ash' search, so Ash on it whiffs. Recognize it as their consistency engine.

Modular field spells. Mignon = player turn ATK boost + Yummy recursion for more Synchros. Acroquey = opponent-turn disruption (destroys cards / summons Yummy from deck when their monsters leave). Acroquey is a backrow threat that survives monster removal.

key_cards.card: Link-1 enablers (Sangan to Salamangreat Almiraj; Sky Striker Hornet Drones / Kagari)
key_cards.role: The true ignition. The whole deck needs a Link-1 on board to turn on its hand-summon and Synchro-via-Link mechanic. Stop the FIRST Link-1 and the combo never starts.

key_cards.card: Baronne de Montmorency / Herald of the Arc Light / Thunder Dragon Colossus
key_cards.role: Generic Synchro end board. Baronne = omni-negate + pop, Herald = omni-negate (sends to GY), Thunder Dragon Colossus = locks special summons from hand/deck for non-Yummy decks. The actual threats you must break.

interruption_points.timing: Before they establish their first Link-1 (Sangan/Almiraj or Sky Striker Hornet Drones token + Kagari)
interruption_points.action: This is the cleanest stop. No Link-1 means Yummy monsters can't special summon from hand and Yummy Way can't be made. Veiler/Imperm the Link-1 or Ash the Sky Striker / Sangan trigger.

interruption_points.timing: On the first Yummy Way Synchro Summon (the resource dump)
interruption_points.action: Ghost Ogre or Veiler/Imperm the Yummy Way on summon to deny the search/draw and the tag-out tuner. Killing the first Way chokes the extension before it snowballs.

interruption_points.timing: On Yummy Snatchy's field-spell search
interruption_points.action: Note: this is a NON-targeting 'no-Ash' search, so Ash whiffs here. Use Droll instead (it stops ALL further adds-from-deck after the first), which is far more punishing to Yummy than Ash.

interruption_points.timing: When 5+ summons hit the board in one chain (climbing to Synchros)
interruption_points.action: Nibiru window. Drop it after their 5th special summon but before they finish the end board. Note they can rebuild via Link Spider + a leftover token/Level 1.

interruption_points.timing: Opponent's turn, when Yummy Ways / Acroquey try to tag out and revive from GY
interruption_points.action: This is the disruption loop. DD Crow / Ghost Belle on the GY revival, or simply bait it out, deny the targets, then push. Acroquey is a Spell, so it survives most monster removal.

hand_traps.why: BEST hand trap vs Yummy. The deck chains searches off Snatchy + multiple Yummy monsters; Droll shuts off every add-from-deck after the first, collapsing consistency. Far better than Ash here.
hand_traps.when: After their first search resolves (ideally after the field-spell add), before they chain into more searches.

hand_traps.why: Yummy floods the board with special summons to climb into Synchros. Nibiru tributes the whole board for a token. They CAN recover via Link Spider, so it is a tempo hit, not a guaranteed kill.
hand_traps.when: After their 5th+ special summon, just before they lock in the omni-negate end board.

hand_traps.why: Negate the FIRST Link-1 or the FIRST Yummy Way on summon to deny the loop. Imperm also doubles as backrow vs going second. Targets the ignition, not the payoff.
hand_traps.when: On the Link-1 enabler or the first Yummy Way Synchro Summon (turn it off before it generates material/cards).

hand_traps.why: Destroys a Yummy Way on summon, or pops the Field Spell (Mignon/Acroquey) to cut their ATK boost / disruption. Flexible into the engine and the spells.
hand_traps.when: On a Yummy Way activation, or on a Field Spell when it is the live threat.

hand_traps.why: Yummy is a pure special-summon spam combo deck, so Maxx C draws you a fortune or forces them to stop short. Standard MD turbo answer; they may run Droll/Ghost Belle to fight it.
hand_traps.when: At the very start of their combo, before the first special summon.

hand_traps.why: Works on GY revivals and deck-summon effects, BUT note Snatchy's field-spell search is a 'no-Ash' add and Cupsy becomes a generic draw off a Synchro, so Ash often whiffs on their main lines. Lower priority than Droll/Nibiru.
hand_traps.when: On a GY-revival / summon-from-deck effect, NOT on Snatchy's search (it dodges).

hand_traps.why: Yummy Ways and Acroquey revive Yummy monsters from the GY on your turn. Banishing a key GY target (DD Crow) or negating the revival (Ghost Belle) breaks the tag-out disruption loop.
hand_traps.when: Opponent's turn, when they target the GY to revive and disrupt.

board_breakers.why: Their end board leans on Baronne + Herald omni-negates. Droplet sends to fuel and negates multiple monsters at once while baiting the negates, since they can only stop one card per negate.
If they pass with monsters in attack position (common when they leave a Yummy Way + negators face-up), it wipes the whole monster zone. Bait one negate with a chaff card first, then resolve.
Excellent going second. Yummy ends on multiple Synchros + field spell + a set; Evenly forces them to one card. Strong because their board is wide, not tall.
Clears the Field Spell (Acroquey/Mignon) and any set 'surprise' before you push, removing their backrow disruption layer so monster removal sticks.
Tribute over Baronne or Herald to remove an omni-negate without triggering it, since tribute is not destruction/targeting they can negate. Best single answer to one big negator.
Their board is full of Light/Synchro fodder; Super Poly fuses away a negator (or two) with a removal that cannot be responded to, sidestepping the omni-negates entirely.
General plan: bait Baronne/Herald with an expendable card, then resolve your real board breaker. Two negates max, so a 3-card push usually gets through.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going first: you do not have to out-grind them, you have to deny ignition. Prioritize hand traps that stop the FIRST Link-1 or first Yummy Way (Veiler, Imperm, Ghost Ogre) and hold Droll for the search chain. Crossout/Called by are common in Yummy, so a second relevant interaction matters. Going second: their end board is WIDE (multiple Synchros + field spell + set), not TALL, which makes mass board breakers shine. Lead with Harpie's Feather Duster on the field spell/set, then a wide wipe (Evenly Matched, Lightning Storm) or Kaiju/Super Poly to remove an omni-negate, baiting one negate before the real push. Watch for the opponent-turn tag-out loop: even a cleared board can revive Yummy monsters off Acroquey/Yummy Ways, so disrupt the GY (DD Crow/Ghost Belle) or close the game the same turn you break.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Yummy as a deck that needs ONE small Link monster to wake up, then it snowballs into a board of negate monsters plus a field spell. As a beginner, your job is to recognize the wake-up moment: the moment they make their first Link-1 (Sangan/Almiraj or the Sky Striker token+Kagari). If you have Effect Veiler or Infinite Impermanence, use it on that Link-1 or on the first Yummy Way Synchro, that is where the combo dies cheapest. Do NOT waste Ash Blossom on their field-spell searcher (Snatchy), it dodges Ash; Droll & Lock Bird is the real consistency-killer because it stops all their searching. If you are going second and they already have a board, do not trade one-for-one, their board is wide so wipe it: blow up the field spell/backrow with Harpie's Feather Duster, then use Evenly Matched or Lightning Storm, or tribute their big negate monster with a Kaiju. Finally, remember they can revive monsters on YOUR turn, so try to win the turn you break their board rather than passing back.

counters.archetype: Fiendsmith (LIGHT Fiend recursion / Fusion-Link engine; usually splashed)
counters.tier: Tier 3 (as a standalone), but it is a meta-defining ENGINE bolted onto Tier 1-2 hosts (Snake-Eyes, Ryzeal, Mitsurugi, Kashtira, Lacrima, Azamina). Treat the host deck as the real threat.
counters.game_plan: Fiendsmith is a compact LIGHT Fiend engine that recurs itself out of the GY to grind out Fusion and Link monsters, ending on Fiendsmith's Desirae equipped with Requiem and/or Sequence for 2-3 quick-effect negates plus targeting protection. It also acts as glue: it converts almost any LIGHT Fiend (or one spare body) into negation, recovery, and extra extenders, so it slots into stronger host decks to add a resilient backup wall and hand-trap resistance. The end result is a board with multiple omni-style negates on Desirae layered on top of whatever the host deck (Snake-Eyes, Ryzeal, etc.) already built.

key_cards.role: Main engine starter. Discards itself to search Fiendsmith's Tract (or Paradise). Revives itself from GY by shuffling another LIGHT Fiend back. Seeing this = full combo incoming.
The single most important card to stop. Searches ANY LIGHT Fiend from deck + discards a card, and doubles as a Polymerization from the GY. Ashing the search cripples the engine.
Common Normal-Summon entry point. On summon sends a Fiendsmith card (usually Fiendsmith in Paradise) to GY, feeding the engine. Veiler/Imperm/Ash bait.
1-card combo enabler. As a LIGHT Fiend special-summoned from GY (discarded), it is effectively a free full Fiendsmith combo. Watch for it being discarded by Tract/Engraver.
Link-1 that tutors/equips and starts the Fusion chain into Desirae. Tributes/equips itself to set up negates.
Link-1 that fusion-summons Fiendsmith monsters and equips to grant Desirae targeting protection + an extra negate.
The end-board centerpiece. Quick-effect negates face-up cards up to the TOTAL Link Rating of Link monsters equipped to it (usually 2-3 negates). This is the wall you must break.
Quick-Play trap-like disruption (banish a Fiend to bounce/disrupt) often milled by Lacrima; gives the deck interaction even through hand traps.

interruption_points.timing: On Fiendsmith's Tract activation (the search)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring. This is the cleanest stop. Tract searches any LIGHT Fiend; negating it denies the engine its tutor and its later Poly. Highest-value Ash target in the deck.

interruption_points.timing: On Fiendsmith Engraver's discard-to-search effect
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom (it adds a Fiendsmith S/T) OR Droll & Lock Bird after their first search to lock out all further adds for the turn.

interruption_points.timing: On Lacrima the Crimson Tears Normal Summon (its on-summon send/effect)
interruption_points.action: Effect Veiler or Infinite Impermanence to negate the on-summon effect, stopping the GY setup before it starts. Ash also works if it tries to add.

interruption_points.timing: On Engraver's self-revive from GY (shuffle a LIGHT Fiend to special itself)
interruption_points.action: Effect Veiler / Imperm to negate the revived body's follow-up, or a GY-lock (Dweller already on board) to deny the revive entirely.

interruption_points.timing: On Fiendsmith's Sequence / Requiem effect (the Fusion into Desirae)
interruption_points.action: Effect Veiler or Imperm on the Link-1 to stop the climb to Desirae. If they have only one extender, this can hard-stop the negate package.

interruption_points.timing: Across the whole combo while monsters keep being summoned
interruption_points.action: Nibiru, the Primal Being once they pass 5 summons (Fiendsmith does a lot of small summons). Wipes the board into a 1-token. Note: some builds (Caesar / Photon Lord lines) can play around Nibiru, so read the board.

interruption_points.timing: On the FIRST GY effect of the turn (Engraver revive, Tract-as-Poly, Lurrie special)
interruption_points.action: Drop a GY-disruptor: Abyss Dweller (lock GY effects) via your own turn, or pre-emptive Necrovalley / Soul Drain. Fiendsmith lives in the GY, so a GY lock is devastating.

hand_traps.why: Best single hand trap. Negates Fiendsmith's Tract search (deck-to-hand) or Engraver's search. Stops the engine's tutoring cold.
hand_traps.when: Hold for Tract activation; if no Tract, use on Engraver's discard-search or any Lacrima add.

hand_traps.why: Fiendsmith is search-heavy (Tract, Engraver, host-deck searches). Drolling after their first search shuts off every subsequent add for the turn, choking both the engine and the host deck.
hand_traps.when: Throw immediately after their FIRST search resolves (often Tract or the host starter).

hand_traps.why: Negates a key monster effect on field: Lacrima on-summon, revived Engraver, or the Requiem/Sequence climb to Desirae. Free to drop (no LP cost).
hand_traps.when: On Lacrima Normal Summon, or on the Link-1 trying to fusion into Desirae if they're low on extenders.

hand_traps.why: Same targets as Veiler but also sets as backrow and negates a column. Strong if going second (column lock) and dodges Veiler-immune lines.
hand_traps.when: On Lacrima or the first big in-archetype monster effect; set it pre-emptively if you suspect a grind game.

hand_traps.why: Fiendsmith chains many summons; it usually crosses 5 special/normal summons mid-combo. Tributes their whole board for one 1/1-ish token.
hand_traps.when: After their 5th summon, before they lock in Desirae. Beware Caesar/Photon Lord builds that play around it.

hand_traps.why: Fiendsmith summons a LOT of bodies during its combo, so Maxx C draws heavily and pressures them to stop short. Banned in TCG.
hand_traps.when: Drop at the very start of their Main Phase before any summon (MD only).

hand_traps.why: Destroys an activating card/effect on field: can pop an equipped Requiem/Sequence as it activates, or hit a key Link before Desirae forms.
hand_traps.when: On the equip/fusion step, or to remove a Link off Desirae to cut its negate count.

hand_traps.why: Negates GY-activated effects. Hits Engraver's GY self-revive, Tract used as Poly from GY, and Fabled Lurrie's special from GY.
hand_traps.when: On the first GY effect (revive / Tract-Poly / Lurrie).

hand_traps.why: Punishes the deck's many special summons by refilling your hand, similar pressure to Maxx C and legal in TCG.
hand_traps.when: Early in their turn before the summons stack up.

board_breakers.why: Best-in-class vs Fiendsmith because their whole board is LIGHT Fiends. Cannot be responded to, dodges Desirae's negate, and eats Desirae/the host's monsters as fusion material (e.g. into Mudragon or Garura). Run Fiend/LIGHT-eating targets.

Negates the effects of multiple Desirae-equipped monsters at once and lowers ATK; sending cards from hand/deck makes it hard for them to counter-negate everything. Strong even through targeting protection on Desirae since it doesn't target.
If you end your turn with an empty field going second, it forces them to banish down to one card. Ignores Desirae negate (no targeting) and blows past the equip-based board entirely.
Going second into a board with monsters in ATK, wipes all monsters (or all backrow). Watch that Desirae can negate it if a negate is still live, so bait first or pair with another breaker.
Less central since most disruption sits on Desirae as monster-equips, but useful vs the host deck's backrow and vs Fiendsmith in Paradise / set traps.

board_breakers.card: Kaijus / Lava Golem / Fenrir-style tribute removal
board_breakers.why: Tribute away Desirae itself, ignoring its targeting protection and negate (tributing is not a targeting destruction). Removes the negate engine, then push.
If they used a hand effect on your turn, steal their Desirae or draw/search to fuel your own breaker package, then run over the weakened board.

counters.going_first_vs_second: GOING FIRST: Your goal is to set up an end board that beats THROUGH Desirae's negates, since Desirae negates up to the total Link Rating equipped (often 2-3). Build resilient interaction (multiple independent negates, not one fragile one) and bait Desirae before resolving your real disruption. Pre-emptive GY hate (Dweller end-board, or maindecked Necrovalley/Soul Drain) is excellent because Fiendsmith grinds from the GY all game. Watch out for Fiendsmith in Paradise as a turn-0 disruptor. GOING SECOND: This is the better position vs Fiendsmith. Lead with hand traps on THEIR turn (Ash on Tract, Droll after first search, Veiler/Imperm on Lacrima, Nibiru past 5 summons) to reduce the board, then break what is left with Super Polymerization (eats LIGHT Fiends), Forbidden Droplet (multi-negate through protection), or Kaiju/Evenly to remove Desirae itself. Sequence your breakers to bait Desirae's negate first, then resolve the real out. Do NOT walk a single removal spell into a live 3-negate Desirae.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Fiendsmith as a "parasite" engine: it is rarely a deck on its own, it is glued onto a stronger deck to add a tough negate wall called Desirae plus recovery from the graveyard. Two cards do almost all the work: Fiendsmith's Tract (a searcher) and Fiendsmith Engraver (the starter). If you only remember one thing: Ash Blossom their Tract. That single negate often guts the whole engine. Their final board is Desirae holding 2-3 negates with protection, but it has two glaring weaknesses, it is a LIGHT Fiend (so Super Polymerization eats it), and it can be tributed away by a Kaiju (which ignores its protection). On your turn, sequence carefully: throw a cheap card first to bait a negate, THEN resolve your real removal. And because the engine lives in the graveyard, a graveyard lock like Abyss Dweller is a nightmare for them. Going second is your friend, lead with hand traps, then break the board.

counters.game_plan: This is NOT a combo deck, it is a control/stun deck. It sets a wall of Counter Traps (Solemn Judgment, Solemn Strike, Solemn Warning, Seven Tools, Imperial Order) and negates every key play you try to make, while Bountiful Artemis draws a card and Meltiel gains LP / pops a card each time a Counter Trap resolves, so they refill their hand faster than they spend it. They grind you out of resources, then win with whatever beaters or Fairy payoff (e.g. Archlord Kristya, Saffira, Voltic Bicorn) is left standing. There is no long combo to interrupt, so the fight is about resource attrition and making them spend negations on bait.

key_cards.role: Engine heart. Draws 1 card each time a Counter Trap resolves. This is what keeps them from running out of traps. Run-3 staple of the deck.
Pendulum enabler. In the Pendulum Zone it removes the LP-pay / discard cost of Counter Traps, letting them fire Solemns and Seven Tools freely. Also searches Counter Traps.
Payoff Fairy. Each Counter Trap resolution = gain 1000 LP and (with Sanctuary in the Sky) destroy a card you control. Turns negation into removal + lifegain.

key_cards.card: Solemn Judgment / Solemn Strike / Solemn Warning
key_cards.role: Core Counter Traps. The actual interruption. Judgment negates almost anything (cost = half LP, often free under Ariadne); Strike negates monster effects/Special Summons; Warning negates summons.
Counter Trap that negates your traps/backrow removal, also triggers Artemis/Meltiel. Lets them protect their own field through your Lightning Storm / Duster.
Continuous trap that negates ALL Spell effects. Shuts off your spell-based board breakers (Lightning Storm, Duster, Droplet, Super Poly) if it resolves. Big swing card.
Win conditions / closers. Beaters or Fairy payoffs that end the game once your resources are exhausted. Kristya also locks Special Summons.

interruption_points.timing: Their Standby/Main Phase, before they set traps
interruption_points.action: There is no combo chain to chain-break. The real 'interruption' is denying their draw engine: stop Bountiful Artemis / Guiding Ariadne from sticking, since that is what fuels infinite Counter Traps.

interruption_points.timing: When they flip a Counter Trap on your key play
interruption_points.action: Bait it. Lead with a non-essential summon/spell so they burn Solemn Judgment / Strike, THEN resolve your real engine into an empty backrow.

interruption_points.timing: When Bountiful Artemis is face-up on board
interruption_points.action: Remove or negate Artemis. Without it, every Counter Trap they fire is pure card minus, so they deck themselves into topdeck mode within a turn or two.

interruption_points.timing: When Imperial Order is active
interruption_points.action: Imperial Order locks all your Spells. Resolve trap-based or monster-effect board breakers (Evenly Matched, Kaiju, Super Poly is a Spell so it gets locked) and force them to pay LP each Standby to keep Order up, or wait it out.

hand_traps.why: Strong but situational. Counter Fairies is a low-summon control deck, so it often only Special Summons once or twice. They can just play around it by passing and setting traps, drawing you few cards. Decent vs their Fairy payoff turn, weak vs pure stun.
hand_traps.when: Going second / on their turn if they start Special Summoning Fairies. Less impactful than vs combo decks.

hand_traps.why: Hits Guiding Ariadne's search and other deck/GY searches, slowing their engine assembly. Does NOT stop the Solemn Counter Traps themselves.
hand_traps.when: On their search effect (Ariadne / Fairy tutors). Activate before they lock in their trap suite.

hand_traps.why: One of the best vs this deck. After their first search, it shuts off all further searching AND drawing for the turn, including Bountiful Artemis draws. Cripples their refuel engine.
hand_traps.when: After they make their first search of the turn, ideally before Artemis-fueled draws snowball.

hand_traps.why: Negate Bountiful Artemis or Meltiel directly so their Counter Traps stop generating value. Imperm also disables a face-up payoff Fairy. Targeted, surgical answers to the engine.
hand_traps.when: On your turn vs Artemis/Meltiel (Veiler), or set Imperm to negate a payoff Fairy or break their board on your turn.

hand_traps.why: Destroys a face-up Bountiful Artemis, Guiding Ariadne (Pendulum Zone), or a continuous trap like Imperial Order, cutting their engine or stun lock.
hand_traps.when: When Artemis, Ariadne, or Imperial Order is face-up and active.

hand_traps.why: Mostly DEAD vs this deck. Counter Fairies rarely Normal/Special Summon 5+ times in a turn, so Nibiru almost never turns on. Do not rely on it.
hand_traps.when: Only if they go off on a high-summon Fairy turn (rare). Treat as a brick in this matchup.

board_breakers.why: Best-in-class here. Going second into their set backrow, it makes THEM banish down to 1 card, and it is a Trap so Imperial Order does not stop it. Counter Traps can't negate it efficiently since it activates in your Battle Phase / End. Wrecks the stun board.

Tributes their beater/payoff Fairy (Kristya, Voltic Bicorn) without targeting via a Spell that resolves on summon, and it is a monster effect so Imperial Order doesn't lock it. Solemn Strike CAN negate the Kaiju summon, so bait first.
Clears their backrow wall, but BEWARE: these are Spells, so they die to Imperial Order and can be negated by Seven Tools / Solemn. Use as BAIT to drain negations, not as your guaranteed out.
Negates their payoff Fairies / monsters; sending cards from hand+field reduces what they can chain. It is a Spell though, so it eats Imperial Order and Counter Traps, use after baiting.
Spell-speed cannot be responded to by most cards, but it IS a Spell, so Imperial Order shuts it off. When Order is not up, it cleanly removes their monsters with no chance for Solemn to chain.
Pinpoint removal for Imperial Order, Sanctuary in the Sky, or a set Counter Trap before you commit. Cheap way to disarm the stun lock; Cosmic banishes so no GY value.

counters.going_first_vs_second: GOING FIRST: You usually want to establish a board and force them to spend Counter Traps reactively. Play around the negates, lead with bait, and try to land disruption that survives (a set Imperm, or a monster they have to deal with). Do not over-commit into open backrow, they will Solemn your best card. GOING SECOND (often preferable vs this deck): You see their set backrow and can break it. Evenly Matched is the dream out, and spell board breakers (Lightning Storm, Duster, Droplet) bait/clear traps, but sequence carefully because Imperial Order and Seven Tools punish spell-heavy turns. Bait negations with a throwaway play, THEN push with non-spell answers (Kaiju, Evenly, monster effects). Their LP is a resource: Solemn Judgment costs them half LP, so aggressive baiting can put them in range of a single big attack.
counters.beginner_explanation: Treat this like a poker bluffing match, not a race. Counter Fairies has no scary combo to stop, instead it sits behind 4-6 face-down traps that negate your good cards one at a time, and refills its hand with Bountiful Artemis. Two simple rules: (1) BAIT FIRST. Play a card you don't care about and let them waste a Solemn on it, then play your real card into fewer traps. (2) KILL THE ENGINE. If you can destroy or negate Bountiful Artemis, every trap they use becomes a pure loss for them and they run out of gas fast. Going second is fine here, you get to see their backrow, and Evenly Matched is your best friend (it makes them throw away almost their whole field and traps can't stop it well). Watch out for Imperial Order, which turns off all your Spell cards, so keep some non-Spell answers (like a Kaiju monster) in reserve.

counters.archetype: Snake-Eye + Fiendsmith (Pyro combo / control with Azamina + Diabellstar engine)
counters.game_plan: Combo deck that recycles 1-card Snake-Eye Ash into Snake-Eyes Poplar to flood Level 1 Pyros, while the Fiendsmith engine (Engraver -> Tract -> Fabled Lurrie) grinds out Link/Fusion bosses. It ends on a multi-negate board: Fiendsmith's Desirae omni-negate, Azamina Ilia Silvia omni-negate (tributes itself), plus S:P Little Knight, Apollousa, and Promethean Princess. The deck is extremely resilient: it has many short, redundant lines and can rebuild through the GY, so trading 1-for-1 is rarely enough.

key_cards.role: Best 1-card starter. Normal Summon -> searches/sets, recycles itself in spell zone via Original Sinful Spoils. Whole Snake-Eye half flows from here.
Searched off Ash; Special Summons itself and searches another Snake-Eye, fueling the Pyro extension and rank/link plays.
Starter/extender. Sets a Sinful Spoils spell/trap; gateway into the Azamina line and into Original Sinful Spoils recursion.
Engine core. Discards itself to add Fiendsmith's Tract; GY effect re-summons itself. Drives the Fiendsmith Link/Fusion chain.
Adds + discards Fabled Lurrie to Special Summon it, giving a free Link material to start the Fiendsmith fusion line.
Fusion boss with a built-in omni-negate by tributing itself. Primary protection layer the combo builds toward.
Main boss: omni-negate that scales with equipped Fiendsmith Link monsters. Centerpiece of the end board.
GY engine glue: banishes from GY to search Snake-Eye Ash, making the deck absurdly consistent and grindy.

interruption_points.timing: On Snake-Eye Ash Normal Summon / its search
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the search, or Imperm/Veiler the Ash effect to cut off Poplar and the whole Snake-Eye extension before it snowballs.

interruption_points.timing: On Snake-Eyes Poplar Special Summon + search
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the Poplar search, or Ghost Ogre the Poplar to deny the second Snake-Eye and stop the Pyro chain.

interruption_points.timing: On Fiendsmith Engraver discard-to-search (Tract) or its GY self-revive
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the Tract add; Effect Veiler / Imperm the Engraver to kill the Fiendsmith Link/Fusion engine.

interruption_points.timing: On Diabellstar set / Deception of the Sinful Spoils activation
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom or Veiler/Imperm to deny the Azamina (Silvia) setup and remove a protection layer.

interruption_points.timing: When they Special Summon their 5th monster building toward boss
interruption_points.action: Nibiru the Primal Being wipes the engine mid-combo, though it is less reliable this format (see hand-trap notes).

interruption_points.timing: On the Fiendsmith Fusion / Desirae summon (final boss step)
interruption_points.action: Veiler/Imperm a key Link body before Desirae resolves, or save a negate for the Desirae summon itself.

hand_traps.why: Hits the most critical searches: Ash, Poplar, Fiendsmith's Tract, Diabellstar/Deception. Single best generic against this deck.
hand_traps.when: Hold for the FIRST important search. On Ash or Poplar going first; on the Tract add vs a Fiendsmith-heavy line. Beware they may bait with a less important search.

hand_traps.why: Negates a key on-field monster effect (Ash, Engraver, Diabellstar) on your opponent's turn without spending a card from deck.
hand_traps.when: Best on Engraver or Ash. Use when you cannot afford the search hitting; weaker vs spell-based steps.

hand_traps.why: Negates a monster effect AND can disable a column of spell/trap; flexible, can be set going second to dodge Crossout/Called.
hand_traps.when: On the first relevant monster effect (Ash/Poplar/Engraver). Set it going second so it survives backrow interaction.

hand_traps.why: Destroys Poplar on its Special Summon, or pops a key continuous/field piece (Field Spell, Original Sinful Spoils in zone).
hand_traps.when: On Poplar's self-Special Summon, or on a recycled Snake-Eye / field spell that enables the loop.

hand_traps.why: Punishes the deck's many Special Summons; either they stop short (weak board) or you draw heavily. Strong vs a full combo.
hand_traps.when: Activate at the very start of their turn before they commit. Watch for them having Ash/Crossout to negate it.

hand_traps.why: Shuts off all further searches after the first add. Devastating because the deck chains search after search.
hand_traps.when: AFTER they make their first search of the turn (e.g., after Ash searches), locking out Poplar/Tract/Original Sinful Spoils.

hand_traps.why: Tributes their developed engine into one token, blowing up the combo mid-line.
hand_traps.when: After they Summon 5+ monsters. NOTE: less popular this format because Azamina Silvia and other plays dodge or pre-empt it; treat as situational.

hand_traps.why: Format-dependent disruption; pairs with Imperm to pressure key targets.
hand_traps.when: Niche tech, only if your build runs it; otherwise prioritize Ash/Imperm/Droll.

board_breakers.why: Negates AND halves multiple monsters at once; great vs a board of Desirae + Silvia + links. Dodges some negates by sending fuel from hand/field.
Going second, forces them to keep only 1 card; demolishes the multi-piece negate board. Best when you have not committed monsters.
Wipes all their face-up attack-position monsters (or all backrow). Strong if they leave bodies in ATK; watch S:P Little Knight banish.
Clears Original Sinful Spoils / Field Spell / any backrow protection, dismantling the recursion engine and set traps.
Uses THEIR monsters as fusion material; spell-speed-4 so most omni-negates cannot stop it. Removes Desirae/Silvia/links cleanly.
Tribute away Desirae or Silvia ignoring their negate, since tribute-summoning over them is not an effect they can negate.
Specifically cited to remove Promethean Princess and other problem pieces by popping a card during your push.

counters.going_first_vs_second: Going first they are scary: they build a full multi-omni-negate wall (Desirae + Silvia + Apollousa + S:P), so as the disruptor you must land an EARLY hand trap (Ash on the first search, or Droll after their first add) rather than waiting, and ideally stack two interactions. Going second is where you win: combine a board breaker that ignores negates (Super Poly, Kaiju, Droplet) or a sweep (Evenly Matched, Lightning Storm, Feather Duster) with leftover hand traps, then push. Save Imperm/Droplet to set face-down so Crossout Designator and Called by the Grave cannot pre-empt them. Do not over-commit monsters before Evenly/Super Poly. Maxx C going first can soft-lock their full combo if they lack an answer.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of this deck as a machine with many small parts that all search for each other. The cheapest way to break it is to jam the FIRST important search with Ash Blossom (call it on Snake-Eye Ash or Poplar), or fire Droll after their first search so nothing else can be added. One negate usually is not enough because the deck rebuilds from the graveyard, so going second bring a card that wipes everything at once: Evenly Matched, Lightning Storm, or Harpie's Feather Duster, plus a removal that ignores their negates like Super Polymerization or a Kaiju. Set your Impermanence face-down so they cannot snipe it. If you are new: hold Ash for their best search, do not waste it on a bait, and going second clear their board before you attack.

counters.tier: Rogue / lower-meta (consistent ladder pick, fringe in top-cut tournaments as of June 2026)
counters.game_plan: Labrynth is a control deck that sets Normal Traps, then uses them to remove your threats and grind you out of resources over many turns. It is NOT a one-turn-kill combo deck; its power comes ON YOUR TURN, reacting to your plays with Welcome Labrynth and floodgate-style traps while Lady/Lovely Labrynth recur traps and search endlessly. It wants to go first, build a backrow, and win the long game on card advantage.

key_cards.card: Lady Labrynth of the Silver Castle
key_cards.role: Main engine boss. Searches a Normal Trap on each of your trap activations, Special Summons itself when you activate a Set trap, and gains targeting immunity while you control Set cards. The card that refills their hand every turn.

key_cards.card: Lovely Labrynth of the Silver Castle
key_cards.role: Fusion/ace boss. Forces opponent to discard, retrieves and re-Sets Normal Traps from GY, and protects/destroys. The grind-game closer that keeps recycling their traps.
Key Normal Trap. Special Summons a Labrynth from deck; if activated while Set, also DESTROYS a card on the field. The card that summons Arianna/Ariane to start everything and triggers Lady's search.
Upgraded Welcome. Special Summons any Fiend from hand/deck/GY (including Lovely fusion materials/Stovie) and bounces a card. Their strongest single trap.

key_cards.card: Arianna the Labrynth Servant / Ariane the Labrynth Servant
key_cards.role: Servant searchers/extenders. Summoned off Welcome, they search Labrynth cards and Set traps from deck when a monster leaves the field, providing consistency and extension.
Hand/extender. Sets a Welcome from deck and protects Labrynth cards from destruction; key combo enabler going first.
Tech trap that copies a Normal Trap from GY (often re-using Welcome or a counter trap). Adds explosive disruption and is a high-value Ash/Imperm target.

key_cards.card: Muckraker From the Underworld / Stovie Torbie / Cooclock
key_cards.role: Fiend toolbox and Lovely fusion enablers; Cooclock bounces to extend, Stovie/Muckraker fuel the boss line and recursion.

interruption_points.timing: On the first Welcome Labrynth / Big Welcome activation (their main turn-1 starter)
interruption_points.action: Negate it. This is the single biggest choke point. If their first Welcome resolves they search and snowball. Ash Blossom or a counter to the Welcome trap usually ends the turn.

interruption_points.timing: On Arianna's / Ariane's search effect after they hit the field
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom the search to deny the follow-up trap and cut their hand refuel.

interruption_points.timing: On Lady Labrynth's search trigger (fires when they activate a Set trap)
interruption_points.action: Ash Blossom or Imperm Lady to stop the per-trap search engine. Without it they run out of cards much faster.

interruption_points.timing: Across repeated searches in the same turn
interruption_points.action: Droll & Lock Bird after their first search shuts off every further add-to-hand for the rest of the turn, gutting the engine.

interruption_points.timing: When they try to recur traps with Lovely from GY
interruption_points.action: If Lovely is summoned, that is the grind engine. Removing/negating Lovely (or Imperm on it) stops the trap recycling loop.

hand_traps.when: On the first Welcome/Big Welcome Labrynth, or on Arianna/Ariane/Lady's search.
hand_traps.why: Best single answer. Negates the deck's search/special-summon backbone. Hitting the first Welcome usually neuters their whole turn.

hand_traps.when: After they make their first search of the turn (e.g. off Arianna or Lady).
hand_traps.why: Shuts down all further adds-to-hand, stopping the search chain that lets Labrynth refuel. Very strong vs their consistency.

hand_traps.when: On Lady Labrynth's search trigger, on Lovely, or set it to also nuke a Spell/Trap column when going second.
hand_traps.why: Negates a key monster effect; the column-set bonus helps you break backrow later. Note: Lady has targeting immunity while they control Set cards, so use it BEFORE they establish Set backrow or on a non-immune target.

hand_traps.when: On Lady or Lovely Labrynth during their turn.
hand_traps.why: Negates the boss engine without targeting (gets around Lady's targeting protection). Good answer when Imperm would be blocked by immunity.

hand_traps.when: Before they start special summoning (cast it early).
hand_traps.why: Labrynth special summons Arianna/Ariane/Lady/Lovely, so Maxx C draws you cards. Less back-breaking than vs full combo decks (their summon count is lower), but still solid value and pressures them to stop short.

hand_traps.when: Rarely the right call.
hand_traps.why: Labrynth usually summons only 2-4 monsters and does most work on YOUR turn, so they often dodge the 5-summon threshold. Low priority; bring better cards instead.

hand_traps.when: On a Set Welcome/Big Welcome before it resolves, or on Lady/Lovely.
hand_traps.why: Can destroy a Set trap on activation or pop a boss monster, denying a key piece. Flexible but lower impact than Ash.

board_breakers.why: Destroys their entire backrow at once for free. Labrynth IS its backrow, so this is arguably the best single breaker. Beware Set traps can chain in response, so they may use one before it resolves.
Going second, wipes all their Set Spells/Traps (or all attack-position monsters). Devastating because Labrynth commits everything to backrow and few monsters. Top-tier answer.
Going second with an empty/near-empty field, forces them to banish down to one card. Crushes a backrow-heavy Labrynth board and sets up the OTK. Classic Labrynth counter.
Sends from hand/field to negate multiple of their monsters (Lady/Lovely) at once, and dodges some trap immunity by not targeting. Strong to push through the boss line.
Targeted backrow removal to pop their most dangerous Set trap (e.g. a Set Welcome or counter trap) before it can fire, weakening the wall preemptively.
Tribute away Lady/Lovely ignoring their on-field protection (Kaiju is a non-targeting tribute), removing the boss so their recursion stalls.
Banish their Fiend boss (Lady/Lovely) as fusion material; spell-speed and the it-cannot-be-responded-to clause dodges their traps. Excellent if your Extra has a usable target.

counters.going_first_vs_second: GOING FIRST vs Labrynth: race them. Build a board and pressure FAST, because Labrynth is a grind deck that wins long games. Don't over-commit into open backrow blindly, but do not durdle, every extra turn favors them. Bait out one Welcome/trap, then push through. GOING SECOND: this is where you punish them. Mulligan toward backrow wipes (Harpie's Feather Duster, Lightning Storm, Evenly Matched). Clear their Set traps, then OTK, they have very few monsters to block damage once the backrow is gone. Evenly Matched is especially brutal when they passed with a wide trap board. Lead with the board breaker, hold a follow-up in case they chain a trap in response.
counters.beginner_explanation: Think of Labrynth as a turtle, not a sprinter. It does almost nothing flashy on its own turn; instead it sets face-down trap cards and springs them on YOU. The danger is the long game: it keeps drawing and recycling traps until you run dry. Two simple rules: (1) If you have Ash Blossom, save it for their first Welcome Labrynth trap or any of their searches, that is the moment that stops their engine. (2) If you go second and see a row of face-down cards, that is GOOD for you, just blow up the whole backrow with Harpie's Feather Duster, Lightning Storm, or Evenly Matched, then swing for game since they have barely any monsters to defend. Don't slow-play them; speed and one big backrow-wipe are your friends.
